The Club plan, as it stands on 2026-09-25
Nine areas · one verdict each · click any chip or flag
Capability map

What a rep club would meet today

Each tile is one area of the Club offer. The colour is the worst thing a club hits there; the stage is where it gets fixed. House league is last by direction.

Blocks a clubWrong or missing, club can limpRough edgesHolds

The club shell

Stage 1

Board roles cannot be assigned from the screen; a volunteer who coaches elsewhere cannot be invited; there is no way to buy Club even when the gate opens; coming back after cancelling restores nothing.

Rep teams & the coach bridge

Stage 2

Club teams have no season rollover and next season cannot exist while this one runs; adopting a standalone coach's portal into the club orphans most of that team's data. The franchise contract itself holds.

Club money

Stage 3

A treasurer cannot finish the allocation loop; every board figure has a confirmed way to be wrong; money moves on one click with no confirmation, no reversal and a race. No build gate guards any club number.

The public face

Stage 4

A rep-only club's page is an empty tournament page: teams are invisible, there is no teams index, and unticking "Listed on /discover" takes down the whole site.

Families

Stage 5

A merge undoes itself, a changed guardian email strands the child, the family page's money disagrees with the Money hub, and the export claims "everything" while holding a fraction.

Venues, scheduling, permits

Stage 6 · permits Stage 10

Three venue books that never check each other, so a rep practice, a league game and a tournament game can share a diamond unwarned. No club calendar. The admin cannot add a game — by ruling.

Tournaments in a club

Stage 7

A club's own team enters its own event in two manual steps; tournament fees never reach the books; a "first tournament setup" banner shows forever for a club that runs none.

Tests, help, demo, design

Stage 8

The club fixture has an owner and an admin and nothing else; the June walk artifacts are the only record; the rep-teams cluster predates the admin design system; marketing promises features that do not exist.

House league

Stage 9 · last

Five of the six June trust defects are still open: messages that email nobody and report success, the vanishing season, dishonest schedules, no payment loop, unescaped emails. Its standalone plan already exists (League Plus).

Stage 2 · the first ruling · it decides half the drawings

Ask 1 · When does a club team's season change, and who presses it?

The plan recommends two things for club seasons. The first is that the club admin gets the standalone coach's Start next season. The second is that a Draft year may run beside the Active one, so next season's tryouts can happen while this season is still going. The first half fits everything built since August. The second half does not do what it hopes, and the code shows why. Both shapes are drawn small below; every specimen after this one is drawn to shape (a).

Findings behind this ask:

What the code says (read 2026-09-28)

  1. The coach's portal has two season states, and it always shows the newest live year. A team is live while it holds a Draft or an Active year. Draft and Active are the same thing to the portal. When a team holds two, the portal shows the newer one. lib/coach-season-view.ts:14-17, 49-82 · lib/db.ts:4419-4431 (getActiveRepProgramYear: newest of draft|active)
  2. All twelve of the coach's tryout tools act on that one year. They cover sessions, candidates, evaluators, the scoreboard, decisions, accept, the report, the rubric and the rest. None takes a year. app/api/coaches/[orgSlug]/teams/[teamId]/tryout-*/route.ts — each resolves getActiveRepProgramYear(teamId)
  3. A standalone team runs next year's tryout after the roll. Start next season creates the new season already live, with tryouts closed, and closes the old one. The portal's own help tells the coach to do it in that order: “Next year's tryout needs a season to live in. If you run tryouts in the summer for the autumn, start the new season first — everything else follows from it.” lib/rep-season-rollover.ts:183-192, 422 · lib/help-content/coaches.tsx:1401-1402 · COACH_SEASON_CLOSE_AND_ARCHIVE_PLAN.md §5 risk 2 (“Start next season is the first real step of the year”)
  4. The two lines that looked contradictory agree. CLAUDE.md says next year's tryout happens after the last game. It does not say before the season closes, and the roll is what closes it. The help line “turn the tryout you just ran into the start of their season” is about each new player's development starting point. It says nothing about when the roll happens. CLAUDE.md (season ruling) · lib/help-content/coaches.tsx:381
  5. One help line is stale. It says a finished season's tryout “stays readable under Tryouts … the whole period between seasons”. Since 2026-08-18 a team between seasons has one page, and Tryouts is not on it. The Stage 2 build's help pass carries this line. lib/help-content/coaches.tsx:4733 · finding S2-03
  6. The club side today: a new year is refused while any year is Active. The year that is created is a blank Draft, with the staff copied and nothing else. Drafts aren't counted, so two can pile up. app/api/admin/rep-teams/teams/[teamId]/program-years/route.ts:64-100

The two shapes, side by side

(a) One model for both kinds of team Recommended

The club admin holds the three doors a standalone head coach holds: Start next season, Close the season and Reopen. They work the same way, carry the same five things, and give the same warning about unsettled money, which never blocks. Tryouts run on the working season.

  • Aug 16Last game. The 2026 Season stays live while the coach settles money, gives awards, collects documents and emails families.
  • Sep 21The club presses Start the 2027 Season. 2026 becomes a record. The roster, budget plan, fee plan, opening balance and each player's history come along.
  • Sep 21 →Tryouts open on 2027. The coach runs them in the portal, and the club sees the same list.
  • OctoberAccepted players join the 2027 roster.
Coaches Portal · 11U AA
2027 Season
Live
Tryouts · 4 applicationsOpen

What it costs: a club whose tryouts come before its last game has to choose. It can start the new season early, and the games the old season still has left can then no longer be scored. Or it can hold the tryout until after the last game. A standalone team faces the same choice today. If that is a real problem for clubs, it is a real problem for standalone coaches too, and the fix should be one change for both kinds of team, not a separate club model.

(b) The plan's draft year beside the live one

The club opens next season as a Draft while this season is Active and runs next season's tryout on the Draft. Draft would be redefined as a “prep” state that the portal treats as not yet live.

  • July2026 is Active, with games still to play.
  • JulyThe club creates 2027 as a Draft and opens tryouts on it.
  • Portal today2027 is now the newest live year, so the coach's whole portal moves to it. The roster, schedule and money read an empty 2027, and the 2026 games still to play have nowhere to go. 2026 isn't closed either, so it isn't on the closed-season page.
  • Draft = prepThe portal stays on 2026, so the coach can't see the 2027 tryout at all. Reaching it needs a year picker in the coach's tryout tools, which the working-season rule forbids and its build guard exists to stop.
Coaches Portal · 11U AA
2026 Season
Live
TryoutsNo tryout this season

What it costs: either a tryout that only the club side can see (the coach's scorecards, evaluators, scoreboard and decision board can't reach it), or a year parameter in a tryout tool, against a binding rule. It also brings back the in-between season state that the 2026-08-18 ruling deleted (“two states, and the middle one does not exist”), and the portal would have to learn it on every screen.

⚖ Ruled 2026-09-28: shape (a). Owner: “I agree with your recommendations.”
Ask 1. Adopt shape (a) for club teams: the club admin holds the standalone head coach's doors, and tryouts run on the working season. A team's first season is started from the team page, and every season after that starts from the last one. Recommended: (a). Whichever is ruled, nothing here draws an “undo the rollover”; the season-close plan (§3.4) deliberately does not build it.

What Stage 2 builds that has no screen

Each of these is in the plan's ledger (§4B). None needs a drawing, and every one needs doing before the Stage 2 walks can pass.

  1. Access from team membership everywhere (B10). Four coach screens and the club's Assistant coaches list still decide from per-season rows, so a coach between seasons is refused.
  2. Team-group scope on money decisions (B11). Payment-request approve and deny, the admin's mark-paid and the allocation edit ignore a member's team-group limit.
  3. A plan gate on the team-link API (B12). Today a League org can create links.
  4. The dev seed (B13). Roster rows with a source the database refuses, coach rows with no team membership. Also: a club coach's Shared Book opt-in is gated on the notes grant rather than head-coach-only, as ruled.
  5. One roster rule and one record rule (B08). The drawings show them; the build writes each once and every club screen reads it: the board, the team page, the past-season list and the past-season page.
  6. The ownership-transfer rewrite and its coverage gate (B04, Ask 2). One migration re-parents every team table, the staff memberships included. A build gate fails when the set of team tables that carry the club's id differs from the set the move carries, so a table added next year can't be left behind silently. Data dictionary in the same change.
  7. The season doors for a club (Ask 1). The club's Start / Close / Reopen call the same roll and the same state changes the portal uses, with the same “who may” answered for the club side. The roll's self-heal never runs for a club team; it refuses instead.
  8. The notifications that ship with Stage 2's events. Stage 1's drawing of the club's notification settings (specimen 12) placed three Rep Teams rows marked “arrives with Stage 2”: a new tryout application, a portal request to join the club (specimen 9), and missing player documents (only if Ask 5 says yes). Stage 2 adds the coach's side too: the club closed, started or reopened a season (specimen 4), and an invitation accepted or declined (specimens 5 and 6). Each row ships with its event, never as an empty toggle.
  9. Tryouts on the live season, server-side (B07). The admin's tryout routes, the accept step, the sign-up switch and the public form all refuse a closed season, and the public page and form use one rule.

Recorded here, decided elsewhere

  • G03, a club's own team entering its own tournament in one click, is listed under both Stage 2 and Stage 7. Recommended: Stage 7, the tournaments stage (Ask 7).
  • The Stage 2 build prompt is not written until these drawings are ratified. When it is, it settles the order against Admin Design Continuity's Part B (the cleanup): Stage 2's redesigned rep-teams screens replace the legacy ones, and Part B skips them, the precedent Stage 1 set.
Stage 2 · formatting check · owner direction 2026-09-28

Stage 2, checked against the Coaches Portal

The Premium Coaches Portal is the formatting benchmark. By the end of this project the product has one written formatting standard, with every exception named. This page records what the Stage 2 drawings were checked against, what changed, the drift found outside Stage 2, the places where the written rules contradict each other, and the nav difference to review later.

Found here:

What the benchmark is

  • The table and list standard and its exception register (approved 2026-09-06; the row-list recipe 2026-09-16): what a column heading looks like, where numbers sit, the one chevron column, when a list becomes cards on a phone, and that delete is never a row action.
  • The portal's shared kit (2026-09-16): cards, eyebrows, chips, figures, the list toolbar, the rail.
  • The page header and section rules: no subtitle line (2026-08-11), the back arrow goes up one level (2026-09-21), and section headings sit inside their card.
  • The type ladder (2026-08-28): eight sizes, each named for its job (32 · 24 · 20 · 16 · 14 · 12 · 11 · 10).
  • Buttons, forms and saving: one lime action per screen, red only for something destructive, a pick-one field is a dropdown, a plain asterisk on required fields, edits save as you go and creating asks, and the "Saved" word fades.
  • Standing house rules: tinted panels retired (2026-09-21); a record is written with hyphens and a score with an en dash (2026-08-19); times as "10:00 a.m."

What changed in the Stage 2 drawings

ElementThe portal's ruleStage 2 now
Links inside table cellsA row that opens has the name as its link and one chevron in the last column, with nothing conditional beside it. Owner 2026-09-28: no action links in cells; they clutter, and the information is enough.Health board: "Invite a coach" and "Start the 2027 Season" are gone; the team name and a chevron open the team. Tryouts: the per-row Extend offer / Accept buttons move into the applicant's panel. Documents: the "⋯" menu becomes a chevron.
Column headingsThe condensed display face, uppercase, in secondary ink. A heading is never the faintest text in its own table.Every Stage 2 table.
NumbersRight-aligned and tabular, with the heading aligned the same way.Roster and Documents on the board.
Groups inside a tableA band row: display face, uppercase, on the paper tone."Boys · 6 teams", "Girls · 3 teams".
Page title and backThe condensed display face at 20. The back arrow sits in the header's leading corner behind a hairline and goes up one level.Team, Coaches and Tryouts pages.
Section headingsA card with its heading inside: 16, bold, sentence case, with a small mono count beside it.The team page's sections and Sign-ups. They were small mono labels above the cards.
Cards8 px corners, a hairline, no shadow. A card that opens something is a door card: the whole card is the link, the eyebrow carries an arrow, and it lifts on hover. No links inside a card.The team page's four figure cards. Roster, Next event and Tryouts are doors; Record is not.
Row actionsDelete is never a row action; it lives in the record's own page.Coaches: Remove moves into the person's page. A pending invitation keeps Resend and Cancel, as the portal's staff list does.
Summary strips and placeholdersA status is said once. Anything drawn beside every row is drawn as many times as the list is long.The board's strip of red chips is gone, and so is the empty "Stage 3" money slot on every row (one note says the column joins in Stage 3).
Phone listsA list that doesn't fit becomes white cards, each with a corner chevron; a worded action becomes a full-width 44 px button.The board and Coaches.
WarningsTinted panels are retired; a status callout is a white card with a coloured edge.The unsettled-money warning, the no-head-coach notice, and the coach's refused-save note.
Header actionsCreate goes in the header, first, in lime. Export goes in the toolbar over what it exports. At most two buttons plus help.Tryouts (Add applicant in the header, Export in the toolbar) and the team page (the two season doors).
RecordsA record takes hyphens (12-8-1).Everywhere in Stage 2.

Drift found outside Stage 2 (recorded, not fixed here)

  • Today's admin restyle draws table headings off the standard (S2-06). The restyle that went out on 2026-09-28 overrides every admin table's column heading with a sentence-case heading in the faintest ink. The approved standard, and the portal, use the condensed uppercase heading in secondary ink. This belongs to the Admin Design Continuity programme. The fix is to drop that one override, so admin tables take the product's heading.
  • Stage 1's drawings on this hub don't meet the benchmark. They use body-face page titles, small mono labels as section headings, 12 px shadowed cards and sentence-case headings. They are left as ratified. The built Stage 1 screens should be measured against the standard in the formatting pass.
  • Members (Stage 1) has a "Manage" button on every row, where the standard asks for one chevron column. It goes on the same list.

Where the written rules contradict each other

To be settled when the product-wide standard is written. None of them blocks Stage 2; each has a recommendation, and they are Ask 8 on the Decisions tab.

QuestionThe two rulesRecommendation
Face for titles and headingsAn admin ruling (2026-09-25) says titles and table headings take the body face. The table standard (2026-09-06) and every built title and heading use the condensed display face.The display face. Read the admin ruling as "not monospace".
Figures in admin tablesOne rule keeps admin figures in monospace. The 2026-09-25 admin rulings say body face, tabular, as the portal does.Body face, tabular. The monospace exception retires as each admin area is restyled.
What a chevron means2026-08-15: "expand in place, nothing else". 2026-09-03 and every list since: "opens".A right-pointing chevron opens; a down-pointing one expands in place.
The chevron on a phone card2026-07-31: decoration, hide it. The table standard and the built lists: a corner chevron, shown.Show it, as built.
What a row's link isTables: the name is the link. Row lists: the whole row is the link.Keep both, written down as one rule per shape. Amended 2026-09-29 (owner): a row that opens, opens from anywhere in both shapes; the name stays the one real link.
Phone card colourThe standard's text says an olive wash. The 2026-09-21 retirement made them white.White. Update the standard's text.
Chip caseA chip in a table row is uppercase. The kit's card chip keeps the words as typed.One chip: uppercase monospace.
Eyebrow inkA card's eyebrow is secondary ink. The admin page eyebrow is tertiary.Keep both, named as two roles: a card's name is read, a page's trail is context.
How long a success notice staysThe "Saved" word fades after about 2.5 seconds. The club's page notices fade after 8.Keep both, named: a word fades fast, a sentence stays long enough to read.

Nav review, noted for later in this project

Owner, 2026-09-28: the club admin groups its nav as dropdowns, and the Coaches Portal as group headers with the links under them. The code has three models, not two:

  • Coaches Portal rail. Overview sits on its own at the top. Five groups follow: Season, Progress, Money, Communication, Team. Each group heading is itself a toggle, with a chevron and its pages listed under it. Every group starts open except Team, and a closed group shows a count. On a phone, the More sheet never collapses.
  • Club admin rail. Static section labels: Programs, Also on your plan, Organization. Each program is a link that shows its pages only while you're inside it. Owner-only areas show as locked rows. On a phone, a program's first screen has an "In ‹program›" row that opens its pages.
  • Tournament admin, inside the same rail. Operations, Setup and Admin groups that fold, and which ones start open depends on the tournament's status.

Recommendation for the review: one model, with the portal's as the benchmark, decided before Stage 8 so the standard can name it. Nothing in Stage 2 changes the rail.

The standard this project ends with

A product-wide formatting standard that builds on the table and list standard and has an exception register beside it. From now on, every stage's drawings are checked against it before you see them, as these were. Drift goes in the register as a fix, and the contradictions above become its first rulings. It is due by Stage 8, the release-readiness stage.

Stage 3a · read first · the code on 2026-09-30

Where the money rows stand today

The plan's money ledger (C01–C19) was written on 2026-09-25. Since then Stage 0 fixed two dead money controls, Stage 1 gave the treasurer a way to create an allocation, and the admin restyle added Budget and Budget vs. Actual to the rail. Every row was re-read against today's code. Only what is still open is drawn. The five rows marked "new" were found in this pass.

Found in this pass

  1. A coach can take back any club payment, including one the club recorded. The portal's Undo on a club bill (added 2026-09-03 so a coach could reverse their own mistaken tap) never asks who recorded the payment. It voids both ledger lines, the club's own included, with no question and no notice to the club. app/api/coaches/[orgSlug]/teams/[teamId]/allocations/[splitId]/installments/[installId]/route.ts:104-162 · finding S3A-01
  2. No money event tells anyone. Nothing in the product fires when the club records a payment, approves or declines a request, or when a coach files one. A coach finds out by opening the Club tab again. lib/notification-labels.ts (no money event in the union) · admin installment and request routes (no notify call) · finding S3A-02
  3. A pending request holds up the coach's payout, not the season. By an owner ruling of 2026-08-17 the end-of-season payout to families refuses while a club request is unanswered, so an open question doesn't vanish into a closed season. The coach's way out is to chase the club or withdraw it. The club is never told, and when the club closes one of its own teams' seasons (Stage 2), the warning counts families' dues only, not what the team owes the club. lib/season-settlement.ts:239-253 · lib/coach-season-settlement.ts:156-165 · app/api/admin/rep-teams/teams/[teamId]/seasons/route.ts:79 · finding S3A-03
  4. The "team ledger" the club opens is a copy of the coaches' money, and its balance is not theirs. The coaches' screens write a line into it as they record dues, payouts, spending and money in, and the club's transfers write the rest. But it runs across every season the team has had and carries no opening balance, while the coaches' Cash on hand is worked out from their own records, season by season, by its own arithmetic. So the club reads a figure close to the team's cash and not equal to it. The same page lets the club try to edit a coach's line (refused) and move money in or out of the team's book (allowed). lib/coach-register.ts (the Register is a view over the coach's records) · lib/coach-register-book.ts:566-640 (club rows derive from the installment and request records) · app/[orgSlug]/admin/accounting/ledger/[ledgerId]/page.tsx · finding S3A-04
  5. "Overdue" has two rules on two club screens. The Upcoming bills panel on Rep Teams counts overdue correctly, in the house day. The allocations list never can. The Overview's "due in 14 days" count is a third reading, and a fair one. The panel is also closed to a treasurer. app/api/admin/rep-teams/upcoming-payables/route.ts · app/api/admin/rep-teams/allocations/route.ts:55-72 · app/api/admin/club-brief/route.ts:159-170 · finding S3A-05
How the drawings use this. Every specimen after this page draws only what is open. The rows 3b and 3c own (C05, C09, C10, C11) and Stage 7 owns (C18) are not drawn. The one place a 3b figure would sit, the Accounting overview's four totals, is left as it is today and named as 3b's.
Stage 3a · specimen 1 of 7 · whole screen, desktop and phone

A ledger: the club's own book, and a team's

It is Wednesday, September 30. Priya Nair is Northfield Minor Ball's treasurer. She opens the General ledger to check September before the board meets, then opens 11U AA's page because the team is paying late. Today she can't reach the team money screens at all, so the "before" frames are drawn as Dana Whitfield, the owner. Today's General ledger names no team on the club's lines, and a team's page offers buttons the server refuses and prints a balance that belongs to nobody. The proposed club ledger names the team on every line and reads the way the coach's Ledger reads: oldest at the top between a Starting and an Ending balance, the toolbar in two decks, the balance at the strip's right edge, compact rows. It is drawn as the Ledger tab of one Accounting page (Ask 2, option B; option A is on specimen 5). The team's page becomes a read-only statement of what passed between the club and the team.

Why it changed

The first drawing against the coach's Ledger, point by point

Ask 6
PartFirst drawing (hub v21)Now: the coach's LedgerWhy the coach's way
Reading orderNewest first, "Brought forward" at the footOldest first, Starting balance at the top, Ending balance at the footA running balance reads down the page like a bank statement. The coach's Ledger was ruled this way, and its export already runs oldest to newest. A treasurer who reconciles against the bank reads in that order.
A Today lineNoneNoneThe coach's Ledger has none either: it was taken out because an overdue or scheduled line carries its own chip, so a second cue for what day it is adds nothing. The club's pending line does the same.
ToolbarOne row: a count, two dropdowns, Search, Payees, ExportTwo decks: the book, Export and the creates on top; four quiet filter pills belowThe top deck never changes; the strip is what narrows. Split by what changes, not by kind of control (your 2026-09-02 ruling).
The balanceThree figure cards above the table"Balance" at the strip's right edgeWhere the coach's Cash on hand sits. The cards restated the table's own ends. A period's totals in and out are the board summary's job (3b), where the club reads them across every book at once.
Amount columnsMoney in, then Money outMoney out, then Money inThe coach's order. One product, one book shape.
SourceA Source columnNo column: the What words say it, the Type filter narrows by itThe coach's Ledger took its source badge out for the same reason: the row already says it.
Row heightStandard rows (36px), caption on a second lineCompact register rows (25–28px), detail on the same lineThe register exception K-01, which the club's book earns for the same reason as the coach's: a month of entries on one screen.
PendingA Pending card that appears when something waitsA Status pill, and a Pending chip on the lineThe coach's Status pill does the same job for overdue and scheduled money.
Voided linesShown in place, struck throughOff the book until Status asks for them, then shown in place, struck throughA void is a correction, not money, so the book opens without it; the coach's book shows no voided line at all. The club keeps them one pick away because whoever audits the club's books asks for them, and when shown they use the void-row recipe (Ask 5d).
Which bookA page under Ledgers, with a back arrowThe Ledger tab is the book; a Book pill switches (option B)Only if you choose option B on specimen 5. In option A a book stays a page under Ledgers.

Coming due: a Due filter in place of “Show all”, and each state said once

Walking Allocations on 2026-10-05, you asked why what falls due later is a small “Show all” link under the table when the Ledger narrows its dates with a filter at the top, and whether the type and sizing match the app. The sizes all come from the app’s type scale, and the chips are the Ledger’s. Four things don’t match. “Show all” is a filter written as a footnote, it can’t be undone, and it spells an installment differently from the table. The state chip repeats the band above it. The head coach sits under the installment instead of the team. And By allocation keeps a note explaining how its rows open.

Ruled 2026-10-05: every recommendation below (owner: “I agree with your recommendations”), and built on dev the same day. Each is a row on the Decisions tab.

  1. CD1 · The Due filter replaces “Show all”. On the toolbar’s one line, right after View (round 2, your note). Next 14 days (default) · Next 30 days · Rest of the season. Overdue and Sent always show. The export writes what the window shows. Recommended.
  2. CD1b · On a phone, Due goes behind the Filter button and View stays out. You asked for both behind it. The Ledger’s Filter holds narrowings only; View swaps which list you read, so behind the button the phone wouldn’t say which view is on, and the count would light up for a switch of view. Recommended: Due only.
  3. CD1a · It shows in Coming due only. This is an exception to “one toolbar in every view”: By allocation lists allocations, and an allocation spans months, so a due window has nothing to narrow there. Shown in both views, By allocation would need a different default, or a paid-in-full allocation would vanish from it by default. Recommended: Coming due only.
  4. CD2 · Each state said once. The State column goes; the red days-late chip moves beside an overdue row’s date. Recommended.
  5. CD3 · The head coach under the team. The sent note stays under the installment and drops the name when the head coach sent it. Recommended.
  6. CD4 · The note under By allocation goes (“A row opens its allocation from anywhere on it; the name is the link.”). Not drawn: nothing else on that view changes. Recommended.

Kept deliberately, from the same check: bold team names (the 2026-10-02 Ledger ruling names Allocations as keeping them) and two-line rows (the table standard sizes a row by what it holds).

Side by side

What each option means, point by point

Ask 2
Option A · pages in the railOption B · one page with tabs
The railAccounting opens to five rows while you're in it; six once 3b adds SummaryAccounting is one row that never opens, and it carries the waiting count
The page's titleThe page: "Allocations", "Payment requests"The program: "Accounting", with the lit tab saying which page
Moving between pages, desktopOne click in the railOne click in the tab row
Moving between pages, phoneFrom the first page only: three taps from anywhere else, through Ledgers (two if the "In Accounting" row went on every page)One tap, from any page
Where a create sitsIn the page header, beside the page's nameIn the tab's own toolbar (the table standard's rule for a page with tabs)
Switching booksA book is a page under Ledgers, with a back arrowThe Ledger tab is the book; the Book pill switches
3b's board summaryA sixth rail entry, Summary, firstThe Overview tab, which already exists from 3a
Next to the coach's MoneyDifferent: a treasurer who also coaches meets one kind of money book two waysThe same: the same tab row, the same Ledger, the same words
Next to the rest of the adminThe same: every program lists its pages in the railAccounting becomes the one program with tabs, so the rule for when a program gets tabs has to be written down (below)
BuildToday's shape; the rail gains two entries and the pages moveThe pages move, plus one Accounting frame with a tab row (the coach's tab row already exists as one component); the rail entry loses its sub-pages; old addresses forward to the tabs
What doesn't changeWhich pages exist and what is on each; who can open them (Ask 1's rule); the Overview's two doors; the Rep Teams team page's door into a team's money; old addresses forwarding.

Recommended: option B, one Accounting page with tabs. Ruled as recommended, 2026-09-30.

  1. Accounting is one book, not a set of separate jobs. Every one of its pages reads and writes the same club money. Recording an allocation received writes a ledger line, approving a request writes one, and the budget allocates to the teams. A treasurer crosses between them in one sitting. The coach's Money is one page with tabs for exactly that reason; its own design notes put it as "a panel here is a tab, not a page".
  2. The phone. A treasurer approves a request or records an e-Transfer from her phone. In A she reaches a sibling page only through Accounting's first page. In B every page is one tap from every other.
  3. One idea, one shape. The coach's Ledger took the word "Ledger" from the club's Accounting on purpose, so that a treasurer who is also a coach meets one word for one thing on both sides. The frame around the word should match too.
  4. The rail stays short and still. One row that never opens, with its count, instead of five or six rows that appear and disappear as you move.

What it costs. Accounting becomes the only admin program with tabs, which is drift unless the reason is written down. Proposed rule for the formatting standard (the Stage 8 nav review): a program whose pages are views of one body of records is one page with tabs; a program whose pages are separate jobs lists them in the rail. The coaches portal already follows it without saying so: Schedule, Roster and Practice plans are rail entries, while Money and Insights are one page each, with tabs. In the admin, Rep Teams (teams, assistant coaches, documents, past seasons) stays in the rail, and no other program changes.

When A would be right. At a club where different people keep the books and run the team billing, each person would live on their own page, and A reads better. The clubs this tier is built for have one treasurer doing both.

Stage 3a · formatting check · done before you see the drawings

Stage 3a, checked against the Coaches Portal

Every Stage 3a "after" frame was checked against the portal's written rules before this page was published: the table and list standard and its exception register, the portal kit, the nine rulings of Stage 2's Ask 8 and the 2026-09-29 amendment (a row that opens, opens from anywhere), and owner ruling P1 (on a phone, a list of short records is one frame). Money has its own benchmark inside the portal, the coach's Money page, and the club's money pages follow it. The first check (hub v21) took only the Register's column words from it. You asked whether the coach's money screens had been reviewed as a whole, and they hadn't, so a second pass the same day (hub v22) read the Money page's own code: its tab row, its Ledger's two-deck toolbar, reading order, row height and column order. The ledger, the two lists and the frame around them were redrawn to it, and the frame became a choice between two options (specimen 5, Ask 2). Three things the drawings need were not in the written rules; you ruled them with the asks on 2026-09-30 (Ask 5d), and the build records them on the standard, shared with the tournament redesign, which draws money tables too.

The rules, and where each one landed

RuleWhat it saysStage 3a

Each now lives in the window the row opens.

(Corrected in the design review; the first drawing had put facts in three eyebrows.)

Ruled for the product-wide standard (shared with the tournament redesign)

  • A void row. A voided line is off the book until the Status filter asks for it; then it sits where it was: struck through in the faintest ink, a VOID chip after its name, the reason as its detail, no balance, counted nowhere. Nothing in the written rules draws one (the coach's book never shows a voided line at all). The tournament redesign will void fees and refunds, so the two programs should agree on one recipe before either builds it (specimen 1).
  • When a program gets tabs (for the Stage 8 nav review). A program whose pages are views of one body of records is one page with tabs; a program whose pages are separate jobs lists them in the rail. The coaches portal already follows this without saying so (Money and Insights have tabs; Schedule, Roster and Practice plans are rail entries). Only Accounting changes in the admin, and only if you choose option B (Ask 2).
  • An empty money cell. The coach's Register leaves the empty side of a Money in / Money out pair blank; the standard's §3.7 says "nothing here" is an em dash. A dash on every row of a paired column doubles the ink and reads as data. Recommended: register the Register's blank as the rule for a paired money column (the club ledger and the team's page follow it), and keep the em dash everywhere else.
  • A band row that carries a total. "Waiting on you · 3 · $555.00" and "Overdue · 2 · $900.00" put a figure in a band's words. The standard has band rows (labels) and closing rows (answers) but not a band that sums. Recommended: allowed, in the band's words, never as a figure column in the band (specimens 2 and 4).

Ruled for the product-wide standard on walk S3W1 (2026-10-01)

  • The button that does something: two looks for one job. The coaches portal draws an action that is not the page's main one (“+ Fundraiser”, “Make a request”) as a white button with a grey border and dark-grey words. The admin draws it as an olive outline with olive words: Add ledger, Send reminders and New payee here, and about a hundred more across the club's screens. The 2026-10-01 design review ruled the outline for the money pages (“an action that opens a window is an outlined button; a door is olive text”), but it weighed the outline only against the product's grey-filled button; the portal's white one was never on the table. And with doors olive too, “go” and “do” now share one colour and differ only by the box. Recommended for the standard: the admin takes the portal's white button for every such action, changed once where the admin draws its outlined button rather than screen by screen, and decided together with the tournament redesign, which uses the same button. Ruled and built 2026-10-01, as recommended: one change, so every admin screen (club and tournament) and the coaches portal’s few outlined buttons now draw it white with a grey edge, at the admin’s own button height, in both themes.
  • No club name above a page title. Accounting, Rep Teams and House league carried the club’s name as the eyebrow over their title, which the bar at the top of every admin page already shows. Owner, 2026-10-01: “we already have it in the nav above.” Removed the same day; a page’s eyebrow is its trail (Accounting · Allocations) or nothing, and a build check keeps the name from coming back. The Overview, titled with the club’s name under the same name in the bar, is now titled “Overview”, as its rail row and as the coaches portal titles its own (owner, the same day).

Drift found outside Stage 3a (recorded, not fixed here)

  • Two words for one thing, one for each side: the club's "Pay Org / Request from Org" and "Deny" against the coach's "To club / From club" and "Declined". The drawings take the coach's words on both sides (the one-spelling rule).
  • "Paid" means two things on the coach's bill today: a coach tapped a button, or the club has it. After Ask 1 it means one: the club has it. The coach keeps the word Paid; "Received" would read on the coach's screen as money the team received.
  • One figure, two names across the two sides of one bill. The club's screens say Collected and Outstanding; the coach's bill says Paid and Left. Both pairs are today's words and each reads right from its own side, so the drawings keep them. Whether the two sides should share one pair is a /marketing call, not a spelling fix. On the club's side the state of one installment is "Received" (it arrived) and the sum is "Collected": two concepts, two words, used the same way on every club screen.
Stage 3a · not drawn · listed so the build carries it

What Stage 3a builds that has no screen

Each of these is in the plan's ledger (§4C) or was found in this pass. None needs a drawing, and each one has to be done before the 3a walks can pass.

  1. One step for every money move. Recording an installment received (the club's), confirming a coach's "sent", approving a request, and each undo or reversal write the stamp and both ledger lines in one database step. Each is refused if someone else got there first, so no orphaned pair of lines is left behind. Today the lines are written first and the stamp second.
  2. A request is decided once. The approve and decline paths change a request only while it is still waiting, and approval keeps its ledger link (so it can be reversed). The club's day, not UTC, for every entry date.
  3. One rule for who may move club money (Ask 1). Record received, confirm, approve, decline, undo, reverse and send reminders: owner, treasurer, or an admin with Accounting. A coach's own record becomes "sent", which writes nothing to the club's books; the coach's take-back works only on their own unconfirmed "sent".
  4. The pages follow Accounting, not Rep Teams (Ask 2). Allocations and Payment requests move under Accounting and check what the person's role can do and whether the plan carries Accounting. The old addresses forward, and Budget's "View allocation" is shown again. In option B, Accounting becomes one frame with the coach's tab row (the component the coach's Money and Insights already share), its rail entry loses its sub-pages and keeps the waiting count, and a book is chosen by the Ledger tab's Book pill.
  5. A team's book is read-only everywhere. Add, edit and void refuse on a team's ledger (they already do); a transfer refuses when either side is a team; an ordinary entry can't be re-typed as half of a transfer; a line written by an allocation, a request or a house-league fee can't be edited or voided on the ledger.
  6. A transfer voids both halves, through the same two-sided void the coach's undo uses.
  7. Team-group scope on money decisions. Approve, decline, record received and undo refuse a team outside a member's group limit.
  8. Ledger figures from every row. The ledger summaries page through all their rows instead of stopping at 1,000; the overview's card and the ledger page print one balance (the book's whole history); the export fetches the whole period, signs amounts and marks voids.
  9. The General ledger is made once. Two first-time requests at once can each create the club's General ledger; one wins.
  10. Payees: list, rename and merge routes for the club's payees (no delete while an entry names one). A general allocation's source entry is checked against the club's own entries.
  11. The notifications that ship with these events (Ask 5c). To the coach: received, undone, approved, declined, reversed. To the club: a coach says a payment is sent, a new request, a request is holding up a payout. Each ships with its event (the Stage 1 rule: never an empty toggle). The Accounting notification rows Stage 1 placed fill in here.
  12. The club's season window counts what the team owes the club (Ask 5b). When the club closes or rolls one of its own teams' seasons (Stage 2), the warning adds unpaid installments and waiting requests to the families' dues it already counts. It warns and never blocks, as ruled.
  13. The build gates. check:club-money-arithmetic (the allocation, team and ledger figures recomputed from rows in a pure module, as the coach's report gate does); a "same figure, one definition" guard for Collected, Outstanding, Overdue and Balance; the transfer-atomicity test. All in verify:changed. 3b extends the first two to the board summary.
  14. The old look's retirement. Stage 3's build deletes the old-look code of every screen it rebuilds: Accounting's, the allocations' and the payment requests' (npm run check:old-look:report lists 12 files today, and the colour-debt list holds accounting, bva and budget). 3a retires the allocations pages, the payment requests page, the ledger page and the overview; Budget and Budget vs. Actual retire with 3b. Each drop is locked in the same change.

Recorded here, decided elsewhere

  • 3b: the Accounting overview's four figures and the board summary (C04), Budget and Budget vs. Actual (C05, C09, C11), the per-team read of the coach's figures D1 describes (allocated, collected, outstanding, requests, cash on hand, labelled "held by the team"), and the money column on the Rep Teams board. Summary joins the rail with its screen (S1-02).
  • 3c: the club's year (C10). Until then "this year" is the calendar year, and a team's lines are grouped by the team's own season.
  • Stage 7: tournament fees reaching the ledger (C18). The Source filter keeps its place (specimen 1).
  • Families' dues reminders. The Accounting overview's "Dues reminders" buttons email every team's families about their dues, with no preview. That is families' money, and each team's dues reminders already run on a schedule. Recommended: they leave the club's Accounting page with the allocation reminders. Stage 5 (Families) decides whether a club-wide family send exists.
  • Words for /docs and /marketing: the three overclaiming lines (C19: "invoices, reconciliation", "track invoices", Budget vs. Actual's "future update"); the coach's "Pay everyone and close the season", which pays families and does not close the season; and every window and notification sentence tagged on the specimens.
  • Ratified 2026-09-30; the build runs as two sessions: CLUB_TIER_STAGE3A_SERVER_PROMPT.md, then CLUB_TIER_STAGE3A_SCREENS_PROMPT.md, after the tournament redesign's Stage 2 is committed. Their definition of done carries the old-look retirement and the gates above.
Stage 3b · read first · the code on 2026-10-05

Where the 3b money rows stand

Stage 3a built the club's books, the allocation and request loop and a team's account with the club. It was committed on 2026-10-01 and walked under §255. It left three things as they were and named them 3b's: the Budget tab, the Budget vs. Actual tab, and the Overview's four figures. Every row 3b owns was re-read against today's code. Five things this pass found are marked "new". Four of them change what 3b should build, and they are put to you as Ask 4.

FixedAdd item works (Stage 0). The club's form never offered Add category; the club renames its shared categories in the Categories panel.— (the panel moves behind Tools, specimen 1)

Found in this pass

  1. A coach's spending meets the plan by its budget word, never by line. Every cost a coach records carries a budget category and a budget word (item), and Budget vs. Actual matches spending to the plan by that word. The owner ruled on 2026-09-09 that a word carries one line on a plan, because a level between word and line "never reached a figure". A club ledger line carries only a free-text category. The plan's 3b list says entries should "carry a budget line" (J4-024). Built that way, the club side would rebuild the very level the coach side retired, and the two Budget vs. Actuals would match spending to the plan two different ways. schema snapshot: accounting_entries (category text only) · rep_team_expenses (budget_category_id, budget_item_id) · design log 2026-09-09 "one word carries one line" · finding S3B-01 → Ask 4a
  2. The club's plan holds spending only, and nobody ruled that. The add-line form passes a fixed "money out" with the comment "A revenue surface would pass 'in'; there isn't one". The migration that gave every budget word a direction says the library "was built for a spending plan", which describes how it was built, not a decision. So a club's sponsorships, grants and fundraising have no line to be read against, and the board summary's income has nothing to compare with. The coach's plan has been revenue-first since 2026-09-12. app/[orgSlug]/admin/accounting/budget/page.tsx:774-777 · supabase/migrations/246_every_budget_item_has_a_direction.sql (header) · finding S3B-02 → Ask 4b
  3. Two rules on one tab. Adding, editing or deleting a budget line, and saving its periods, check for the owner or the treasurer by name. The Allocate page refuses anyone else. The route behind it answers 3a's one rule (owner, treasurer, or an admin with Accounting), so an admin with Accounting is offered a page that turns them away, and can bill teams but can't plan. budget-plan/lines/route.ts:24 · lines/[lineId]/route.ts:26, 103 · lines/[lineId]/periods/route.ts:28 · budget/allocate/[lineId]/page.tsx:141-149 · …/allocate-to-teams/route.ts:47 · finding S3B-03 → Ask 4d
  4. The coach is never told what the club reads, and 3b makes the club read more. D1's per-team read adds one figure from the team's own books, its cash on hand. The club's "What the club sees" panel on a team's page doesn't list it, and nothing in the Coaches Portal says what the club can read at all, apart from the payee picker's note about shared payees (Ledger Parity). app/[orgSlug]/admin/rep-teams/teams/[teamId]/page.tsx:509-545 · app/[orgSlug]/coaches/teams/[teamId]/accounting/club/panel.tsx (no such line) · finding S3B-04 → Ask 4c
  5. A team's standing has two homes with two arithmetics. 3a put what each team owes the club on the Overview, the allocations and the team's account, all from the one definitions module. Budget vs. Actual's "Team Collection Health" still works it out itself: allocations from every year against this year's collections, "Behind" under 50% collected, and each card opens the whole Rep Teams board rather than the team. The one-definition guard already names this route as 3b's. app/api/admin/accounting/budget-vs-actual/route.ts:91-123, 263-294 · budget-vs-actual/page.tsx:575-647 · tests/unit/club-money-one-definition-guard.test.ts (NOT_YET) · finding S3B-05

Also seen, and not 3b's: the coach's empty Club tab still tells a coach to "mark each installment paid as you pay it" and says only the club's "owner or treasurer" bills. Since 3a the coach says "We've sent it", and an admin with Accounting bills too (club/panel.tsx:565-567). Listed for /docs and /marketing on the Not drawn screen.

How the drawings use this. Every specimen after the next screen draws the rows above. Each of the four findings that changes the build is drawn to its recommendation, so the drawings show what saying yes looks like, and the asks are on the Decisions tab. The club's year itself (its name, months, year-end and carry) is 3c's, and where a drawing needs it, it says so.
Stage 3b · read second · one definition per figure

Each figure's one definition

Every money figure drawn in 3b, with the one sentence that defines it, the competing definitions it replaces, and where it shows. The build writes each into the club's money definitions module, and the arithmetic gate recomputes it from rows, so a figure with no sentence here can't be built. Where a definition is 3a's, it is reused unchanged.

FigureThe one definitionReplaces today'sShows on
PlannedWhat a budget line plans for the year: its amount. A band's total is the sum of its lines. One word (category and item) carries one line, so planning a word already on the plan adds to its line."Total Budgeted" on Budget and "Estimated" on Budget vs. Actual: one sum with two names.Budget · Budget vs. Actual ("Budgeted", the coach's column word) · the summary
AllocatedWhat the club billed its teams from a line: the teams' shares of every allocation drawn from that line, added up. A line can carry any number of allocations.One allocation per line (a second is refused, and the reader keeps one); the allocation's own total recorded as the line's total even when the shares add to less (C11).Budget · Allocations (3a, unchanged) · the teams
Not allocatedPlanned − Allocated on a cost line: the part the club pays itself unless it allocates it later. Never below zero, because a line can't be planned below what is allocated.Four names for one thing: "Unallocated Budget" (Budget's card), "Unallocated" (Budget vs. Actual's column), "Org retains" (the allocate review, which reads as money the club keeps) and the code's "orgHeadroom".Budget, under a line
CollectedSaid by where it sits, as the coach's screens already do. On Allocations, a team's account and the Budget's column: what the club has received against allocations (3a's definition, unchanged). On Budget vs. Actual's band: the Actual of Total revenue, every money-in line posted in the year on the club's Club books, received allocations included.Four "Collected from teams" (the Budget card over all years, team health over one year, the allocations list all-time, the old overview never). Approved To-club requests were in none of them.Allocations · Budget · Budget vs. Actual · the summary
OutstandingBilled − collected, across every year, as of today: installments the club hasn't received. A payment a coach says is sent is still outstanding until the club confirms it (3a).— (3a's, unchanged)The summary ("Owed by the teams") · the teams · a team's account
ActualFor a line: posted lines in the year on the club's Club books (the General ledger and any book it opened by name) that carry the line's budget word, money out for a cost and money in for income. Pending and void lines count nowhere. A line written by the money loop files itself: an allocation received under "From the teams", a request paid to a team under "Team support", money received on request under "From the teams, on request".No Actual for any line (C09, J4-024); "Org Ledger Expenses", the expense lines of the club's books, newest fifty only (C05).Budget vs. Actual
SpentThe Actual of Total expenses: every posted money-out line in the year on the club's Club books, on the plan or off it, money paid to teams on request included. A transfer between the club's own books is not spending. A tournament's and the house league's books keep their own money until Stages 7 and 9 decide how it joins the budget."Org Ledger Expenses" (the cap, and requests paid to teams left out).Budget vs. Actual's band · the summary
Off-planSpending on a word the year's plan has no line for, plus spending filed to no word yet ("Not filed"). The coach's "nobody budgeted this". Hidden at zero.— (new)Budget vs. Actual's band · the summary
HeadroomOne: planned expenses − Spent, for the year. Said once, on the summary. Budget vs. Actual says the same thing as "Spent $X of $Y planned", as the coach's band does since Headroom left it (2026-10-01).Budget's "Unallocated Budget" (planned − allocated) and Budget vs. Actual's "Org Headroom" (planned − ≤50 expenses): one word, two sums (C05).The summary
Cash on hand · the club'sThe Balance of every book the club owns (Club, Tournament and House league kinds) added up: posted, whole history, as of today. Never a team's book. A pending cheque doesn't move it; it is a caption."Net position": income − expenses across every book, the teams' included, for a From/To period (C04).The summary · Budget vs. Actual's band
Owed by the teamsOutstanding across every team, as of today. Its caption says how much is overdue and how much is sent and waiting for the club.— (the club had no receivables figure)The summary
Waiting on youRequests still waiting for the club's answer: their count and their total, both directions together ("how much is waiting on me", not a balance).The morning brief's count (unchanged), now with its money.The summary
Cash on hand · held by the teamThe coach's own Cash on hand for the team's live season: the figure the coach's Money shows, read when the page loads and never stored by the club. A team with no live season shows its last season's closing figure and that season's close date. Labelled "held by the team", never added into a club figure, and totalled only in its own band.The team-book copy's balance (S3A-04), which 3a stopped showing.The summary's teams · a team's account
Net for the yearTotal revenue − Total expenses, planned and actual. The coach's "Season net", in the club's unit.— (new)Budget · Budget vs. Actual · the summary
Opening balanceWhat every book the club owns held at the start of the year's first day: the posted lines dated before it, added up. Worked out from the books, never typed (a coach's season carries a typed opening because its records start fresh; the club's books never do). Until 3c it is Jan 1; 3c moves the day and locks a closed year, so a line backdated into it can't move the figure.“Opening and closing balance join with the year-end carry (3c)”: no opening at all.Budget (List and By period) · Budget vs. Actual › Months
Closing balanceOpening balance + the net, every book the club owns. On the Budget, the plan's: the year's Total revenue − Total expenses added to the opening. On Months, each month's opening + its net; under Cash, this month closes on Cash on hand to the cent.“Net for 2026” as the plan's close.Budget · Budget vs. Actual › Months
The club's other booksOn Months: what a tournament's or the house league's book took in or paid on its own in the month, transfers between the club's books left out. One row, so a month's balance covers every book while the statement above it reads the Club books. It leaves when Stages 7 and 9 bring those books into the budget.— (new)Budget vs. Actual › Months
The year ruleAn allocation belongs to the year of the line it was drawn from, and one made without a line to the year its first installment falls due. A year's Allocated, Collected and Outstanding read the same allocations. A ledger line belongs to the year its date falls in. Until 3c names the year and sets its months, a year is the calendar year.Team health: allocations from every year against collections from one, so a team with nothing due reads "Behind" (C09).Every 3b screen
The one place two scopes share a word. "Collected" means the allocation figure on the loop's screens and all money in on Budget vs. Actual's band. The coach's screens already do exactly this (dues on Player Dues, all income on Budget vs. Actual), and that was accepted when the coach's band was ruled on 2026-10-01. Following it keeps the two Budget vs. Actuals reading the same. It is named in Ask 2, so the choice is made on purpose. In the code the two are two functions with two names, and the one-definition guard holds each surface to its own.
Stage 3b · specimen 1 of 6 · whole screen, desktop and phone

The Budget: a plan the club can keep billing from, and plan a year ahead

It is Wednesday, September 30. Priya Nair, Northfield's treasurer, is getting the 2026 budget ready for the board and wants to start 2027's. Diamond permits were planned at $14,000. In July the club billed the teams $12,150 of that, and the other $1,850 is still on the line. Today the Budget can't bill that $1,850 (a second allocation from a line is refused), can't open 2027, plans spending only, and calls the unbilled part four different names. The proposal is the coach's Budget with the club's one difference, billing teams, built into the line: the coach's revenue-first grammar, a column for what was allocated and collected, a line that opens to read and edits as a whole, and next year one pick away.

What else in 3b reaches the coach: nothing

Stage 3b · formatting check · done before you see the drawings

Stage 3b, checked against the Coaches Portal

Every 3b "after" frame was checked against the portal's written rules before this page was published: the table and list standard and its register, the portal kit, Stage 2's nine formatting rulings with the 2026-09-29 amendment, and every ruling since 3a was drawn (the list is below). The coach's Money is the benchmark for money, and this time its two screens were read in their own code before drawing. The Budget panel was read for its band, its List / By period view, its revenue-first ladder and its When column. The Budget vs. Actual panel was read for its band, its Statement, its Compare and its phone table. Ask 2 is that comparison, put as a question.

The rules, and where each one landed

RuleWhat it saysStage 3b
The coach's money bandEvery money tab opens on MoneySummaryBand: up to four tiles, a label in capitals, a figure, a caption; colour only where it is a verdict; two-up on a phone, never orphaned.Budget (Total revenue · Total expenses · Net), Budget vs. Actual (Collected · Spent · Off-plan · Cash on hand, the coach's own four), the summary (Cash on hand · Owed by the teams · Waiting on you). Today's figure cards go on all three tabs.
A money report's shapeThe coach's Statement: Revenue then Expenses, categories folding to lines, a total per band, closing on the net; Budgeted · Actual · Variance, Variance a word; Compare: whole season or to date.Budget vs. Actual's Statement in full, and its Months view (Ask 5): the coach's month grid with four of its five lenses. The Budget's List and By period both close on the coach's Opening balance · Net · Closing balance. By activity waits for Stage 7.
One toolbar in every view (2026-10-01)A screen's toolbar is the same line whatever view is on; rare tools sit behind Tools.Budget: Year · View (and When, while a line has no date) · Export · Tools · Add line in both List and By period, the Ledgers' order (2026-10-02), with Categories and teams' words behind Tools. Budget vs. Actual: Year · View · Compare · Collapse all · Export on the Statement; on Months, Showing takes Compare's place, the coach's own ruling (2026-09-04), so the line keeps its shape; Collapse all stays (2026-10-07, both portals).
Buttons (2026-10-01 and 10-03)Every admin action is the portal's white button, 34px on a computer; one lime per screen for the main create; a toolbar door is a button; a card-foot door is olive text.Lime: Add line, Start from 2026's plan, Next: team splits, Add entry. White: Tools, Export, Allocate $1,850.00, Add ledger. Olive text: "Budget vs. Actual" at the foot of the summary's year card.
Export is one button (2026-10-01)No chevron; Excel is the menu's first row; a 44px icon on a phone.Budget, Budget vs. Actual, the summary (the board report), a team's account and the payee report.
A record reads first (2026-10-01)A record opens to read; one head pencil turns all of it into its form, ✓ in the same spot turns it back; edits save as you go with the floating pill.A budget line. Its allocations are a section of the record, and Allocate is an action, so it works in both modes.
No controls in a cell; the row opensThe name is the one real link, the whole row opens, one chevron at the end; delete is never a row action.The Budget loses View Allocation →, Allocate to Teams, ✎ and 🗑 from its rows. On Budget vs. Actual a row opens nothing and its two figures are the doors, as on the coach's (2026-09-10); a payee report row only folds.
Chevrons (ruling 3)Right opens; down expands in place.Category rows and the payee report's teams fold in place: right while folded, down while open, as the coach's categories do. A chevron at a row's end points right and opens.
Money cells (3a's Ask 5d)A dollar sign in every figure; the empty side of a money pair is blank, not a dash; a band row may carry a total in its words.Blank Allocated and Collected on a line the club pays itself, and on the revenue band. An off-plan row's Budgeted is the coach's amber dash: it means nothing was planned, not the empty side of a pair. "6 teams recorded · $3,240.00" on a phone band. The two month grids print the coach's grid notation: whole dollars, no sign, brackets below zero, a dash for nothing (see the drift note).
A status said onceA chip only where it adds something.No chip and no word on an off-plan row: the amber dash says it, the coach's rule (the "not planned" word was removed 2026-09-04, the tint 2026-09-05). A red caption on a late team. No row counts its lines (2026-09-04, guarded on the coach's side).
A waiting count (2026-10-01)The rail's amber pill, never words added to a name.The summary's Requests column and the phone rows. Waiting on you's figure is amber, as the coach's "Waiting on the club" is.
No club name above a title (2026-10-01)The bar already shows it; a page's eyebrow is its trail or nothing.Every frame titles "Accounting" with nothing above it; pages one level down carry their trail (Accounting · Ledger · Payees).
Phone lists (P1) and the phone reportShort records in one frame with hairlined rows; a labelled record is a card; a money report keeps its columns and scrolls under a pinned first column.The summary and the payee report: one frame. Budget and Budget vs. Actual: the coach's scrolling tables, names pinned, categories kept as rows. Months too, opened on this month.
CalloutsTinted panels are retired; a callout is a white card with a coloured edge."Held by the team" in blue on a team's account and the payee report. The same edge marks the held-by-the-team figure and band; the teams table’s column carries the lock and the words, not an edge (2026-10-07). The coach's Club tab says what the club sees in one quiet line at its foot, not a card.

A new shared table part, put as an ask

  • A column the screen reads but doesn't own (Ask 4e). The summary's "Cash on hand · held by the team": a lock and the owner's name in its heading, the table's closing row left blank under it so it is never added into the club's totals, and its own total in a separate band worded as not the club's. No written rule covers a figure a table shows and doesn't own. The tournament redesign draws tables too: a team's entry fee read from its coach is the same case. Tagged "shared — the tournament redesign draws tables too".
  • Not new: the Year pill. It is the scope picker the tournament admin already leads its toolbar with, worn by the coach's View pill. The one new thing is that its menu always offers next year.

Design pass, 2026-10-05 (before you rule)

A /design pass read every 3b frame against the coach's own Budget and Budget vs. Actual code and the rulings behind them. Where a drawing had drifted from the coach's screens it is redrawn, listed here. No ask's recommendation changes; Ask 2 gains a sixth named difference and Ask 4c moves its sentence.

  • The Budget's revenue is grouped by category, as the coach's plan reads it (the category is the shelf, 2026-09-09), in the coach's money-in green. "From the teams" leads and counts its allocations, without the "read only" tag; its Collected stays on the cost lines it was billed from, so the teams' $12,000.00 shows once.
  • No row counts its lines. The "1 line" and "2 lines" captions are gone from both tables: the owner removed them from every coach surface on 2026-09-04, and the coach's build guards it.
  • No "Not in the plan" chip on Budget vs. Actual. An off-plan row shows an amber dash in Budgeted, the coach's rule since the owner removed the word (2026-09-04) and the tint (2026-09-05). Item captions went the same way: the pending cheque is a note under the table, and the panel behind a figure names the requests.
  • From the teams' allocations are ordinary lines on Budget vs. Actual (they were small grey sub-rows), names are not links (the figures are the doors), and every line's Variance takes its colour, as the coach's do.
  • Toolbar order: Export · Tools · Add line, the Ledgers' order (2026-10-02); When joins the Budget's toolbar while a line has no date, and "No date yet" takes the coach's amber.
  • The Budget on a phone is the coach's table, scrolling under pinned names with its categories as rows. The card per line lost the categories and clipped "$1,850.00 not allocated" to "not". Budget vs. Actual's phone now starts on Revenue and keeps its categories too.
  • New allocation is a page, as 3a built it, opened from the line and filled in from it; it was drawn as a window.
  • A held edit says why once. The admin kit's save pill carries the held reason, so the red line under Planned went.
  • Add an entry is 3a's window as built (What, Reference, Status and Notes were missing); only Category → Filed under changes.
  • The summary. 9U A's waiting request was missing (three wait, $555.00: 9U A, 12U AA and 13U AA, as in 3a's specimens), and it is the one holding up a payout. The headroom sentence states its arithmetic (revenue $14,280.00 under plan, $10,890.00 of it owed by the teams) where it said "most of the shortfall". On a phone each team's cash carries "Held by the team", because a phone has no column heading to carry it, and "Owed by the teams" is spelled as on a desk.
  • The Rep Teams board's column is "Outstanding", the summary's word for the same figure.
  • The payee report: every team folds, so the names line up; the phone lists the teams in the desk's order and folds too.
  • The coach's Club tab: the sentence moved from a card under the band to one quiet line at the tab's foot. A coach comes to pay the club, so the bills lead and reference goes last (2026-09-06), and a standing card above the work is text read past every visit (the owner's own reason, 2026-09-04).

Drift found outside 3b (recorded, not fixed here)

  • The coach's empty Club tab still describes 3a's "before". "Mark each installment paid as you pay it" (the coach now says "We've sent it") and "your club's owner or treasurer splits a shared cost" (an admin with Accounting does too). For /docs and /marketing.
  • The Payee window is an always-editing form. The 2026-10-01 standard says a record reads first and edits whole, and named the club's Payees window among those that should follow it. It still opens as a form. Ledger Parity's to judge; 3b only adds a door to it.
  • The coach's two month grids print without a dollar sign, against the written money-cell rule ("a dollar sign in every figure"), and no exception-register row says so. The club's copy them (a twelve-column grid needs the room). Recommended: a register row for the month grids, in the 3b build's first part, rather than a sign in every cell. Ruled 2026-10-06 as recommended.

What Stage 3b builds that has no screen

Each of these is in the plan's ledger (§4C), in 3a's "kept for 3b" list, or was found in this pass. None needs a drawing. Every one has to be done before the 3b walks can pass.

  1. The entry ↔ budget word link (Ask 4a). A club ledger line gains the coach's two columns, a budget category and a budget word, from the one budget library; the add and edit windows' Category becomes Filed under. Lines the money loop writes file themselves: an allocation received under "From the teams", a request paid under "Team support · Paid to teams on request", money received on request under "From the teams, on request". The free-text category retires into the budget's categories, so the Ledger's Category filter lists those, never a team's words (C14). Old lines keep their words and read Not filed. A migration, the dictionary and both snapshots in the same change.
  2. One word, one line on the club's plan (Ask 4a). The coach's mig-286 rule for club lines: planning a word already on a year's plan adds to its line. Count the twin lines on dev and prod BEFORE writing the join, as the coach's migration did, and read every foreign key's ON DELETE first (a join is destructive in two directions).
  3. Many allocations per line (C11). Drop the "already allocated" refusal. The plan reader adds up every allocation drawn from a line. An allocation's total is its teams' shares. The allocation and its link to the line are written in ONE database step (3a's pattern), so a half-made allocation can't be billed again. A line's total is refused below what is allocated, with the figure. Periods are editable at any time and every save is checked. The old Allocate page retires into 3a's New allocation, which reads the line's own year (C10).
  4. Revenue on the club's plan (Ask 4b). The add-line picker offers money-in words as well as money-out ones; "From the teams" is worked out from the allocations, never stored; the plan's export and Budget vs. Actual's export gain the Revenue band.
  5. One definition per figure, and the gates. Planned, Allocated, Not allocated, Actual, Spent, Off-plan, the one Headroom, the club's Cash on hand, Owed by the teams, Waiting on you, Net and the year rule go into the club's money definitions module. check:club-money-arithmetic recomputes Budget vs. Actual's and the summary's figures from rows. The budget-plan and Budget vs. Actual routes leave the one-definition guard's "not yet" list (it only shrinks). The summary reads Budget vs. Actual's report, never a second computation.
  6. The per-team read of a team's cash (D1). A club route reads the coaches' own Cash on hand for each team's live season, through the coach's own function, never a year parameter into a coach route (CLAUDE.md's look-back rule), and a closed season's closing figure for a team between seasons. Group scope applies. It is never stored, never in a club total, and totalled only in its own band.
  7. The board summary's read and its export, the board report in Excel and PDF, with the team cash labelled exactly as on screen.
  8. The shared-payee report's read. Mig 316's data and the plan's definition, word for word: the two stamps, the payment date in the year, Ask 3's team list, "Nothing recorded". Nothing on the Payees list changes.
  9. Budget's writes answer the one money rule (Ask 4d): lines, periods and allocate all ask the same question 3a's routes ask.
  10. The month grids' club feed (Ask 5). Budget, Scheduled, Cash and Difference by month for the Club books; the opening balance worked out from every book on the year's first day; the other books' row; the twelve-month window. check:club-money-arithmetic proves every column's opening + net = closing and that the Cash lens's closing for this month is Cash on hand. The grid itself is the coach's, fed the club's figures, never a second grid.
  11. The ledger summary as one database sum, replacing the page-by-page walk 3a kept on purpose for 3b.
  12. The old look's retirement. 3b retires the Budget page and its stylesheet, the old Allocate page, and the Budget vs. Actual page and its stylesheet (npm run check:old-look:report; the colour-debt list names budget and bva), the dead "Coming Soon" window with them. Each drop is locked with --init in the same change.

  14. No new notification. Nothing in 3b is an event: planning, reading and reporting tell nobody anything.
  15. Walks §F on the ledger, written as checkable walks on this hub's QA tab, one purpose each.

Recorded here, decided elsewhere

  • 3c: the year's name and first month, the year-end lock (which fixes a closed year's opening balance, so a backdated line can't move it), this year against last year, the year-end statements an annual meeting reads, archiving a finished year's books, the year a page opens on, and New allocation offering only open seasons (C10).

How a team's season meets the club's year

A season stores no dates. It is a year number ("2026"), a name ("2026 Season") and a status; it begins whenever the club starts it and ends whenever the club closes it, and neither moment is kept . So the club's year can never ask which season a date belongs to, and it doesn't need to: an allocation takes its year from its budget line and its season from each team's split, and each payment lands in the books on the day it arrives. Below is the test club's 13U AAA as the code holds it today (built 2026-10-07), laid over a club year that starts in September.

SONDJFMAMJJASONDJFMAMJJA Club year 2025–26 · Sep 1, 2025 to Aug 31, 20262026–27 · Sep 1, 2026 to Aug 31, 2027 13U AAA seasons 2026 Season · live from last fall's roll until the club closes it2027 Season, once the club starts it Diamond fees 2026 billed from 2025–26's plan (the permits, Apr to Jun 2026), so it counts in 2025–26Aug 23Sep 22Oct 17 Fall ball fees from the same line, so also 2025–26'sNov 6

Gold marks are installments due, from the fixture. The roll date is drawn where a club would start next season; the code keeps none.

  1. Where the season straddles. 13U AAA's 2026 Season runs from last fall's roll to this fall's, so it lives in both club years. Diamond fees 2026 counts in 2025–26, the year of the line it was billed from, on the Budget's Allocated and Collected; two of its three payments arrive in September and October, so on Budget vs. Actual they are 2026–27 money. Nothing is wrong with that: Budget vs. Actual counts money in the year it arrives, as it does today for a December installment paid in January. Specimen 4 names it on its own line, so the board can see last year's bills in this year's revenue. lib/club-money-figures.ts allocationYear · lib/club-budget-report.ts allocationInYear · rep_allocation_splits.program_year_id (the split's season)
  2. Where it bites. In October the club bills next year's costs, and New allocation offers each team its open season. In October that is the 2026 Season, the one that is ending, because the 2027 Season doesn't exist until the club starts it. So 2026–27's bills land on 2026 seasons, and when the club rolls those seasons over, the coach's Club tab stops listing the bill while it is still owed . This happens today with a January year too; a September year makes it the ordinary case. Put to you in Ask 8. app/api/coaches/…/allocations/route.ts:28-37 (the working season only) · lib/db.ts:14267-14276 (.eq program_year_id) · club/panel.tsx:59-63 "SEASON-SCOPED, BOTH HALVES"
  3. What doesn't need deciding. Which club year a season "belongs to". The season is the team's container from roll to roll and the coach's rules stand; the club's year is read from the line and the dates. No specimen asks a season for its year.

What "ledgers archive at year-end" can mean

  1. Nothing archives a book today. A book has an "archived" flag that no screen or route ever sets, and the year's report reads every club book whether or not it is set. accounting_ledgers.is_archived (dictionary: "write-never … archiving unimplemented") · lib/db.ts getClubOwnedLedgers (no filter on it)
  2. A club book runs across years. The General ledger is the same book in 2025–26 and 2026–27; the year's opening is worked out from it. Archiving it at a year-end would hide this year's lines along with last year's. What a year-end needs is last year's dates locked on every club book, which is Ask 1 and Ask 2 .
  3. Where archiving does make sense: one kind of book, a finished tournament's ("Harvest Classic 2025"), whenever its event is over, not at a year-end. A tournament's money is Stage 7's. Recommended: strike the line from 3c, and give "archive a finished tournament's book" to Stage 7.
