Why the club's year is not a coach's season

  1. The coach's ruling exists to stop a year reaching thirty screens. A season owns the roster, the practices, the games, the tryouts and the money, so a finished season shown through the ordinary screens taught every one of them to read a year, and 17 read-only branches followed. The build now fails when a coach route or page learns to read a year. That guard reads only the coaches portal's routes and pages; the club's money routes have taken ?year= since 3b. CLAUDE.md, "A season is live until it is closed" · tests/unit/coach-history-endpoint-guard.test.ts (rules 1 and 2: app/api/coaches and the coach pages only)
  2. On the club side only the money tabs read a year, and they already do. The Year pill leads the Budget, Budget vs. Actual and the Overview, and the three remember one choice per visit; the payee report reads it too. The Ledger reads a date window, and Allocations, Payment requests and Coming due read today. Option 1 adds no year to any screen that doesn't have one. components/admin/kit/club/money/YearPill.tsx (header) · useClubYear on the three tabs · lib/club-money-figures.ts readYearParam
  3. The lock rides a switch the screens already have. Every Budget read already carries the server's answer to "can this person write here?", and the page renders Add line, the line's pencil and Allocate only when it says yes. A closed year is that answer saying no, with the reason. That is the coach's own rule (absent, never greyed) with no new read-only branch on a screen. app/[orgSlug]/admin/accounting/budget/page.tsx:163, 279 (canMove) · BudgetWindows.tsx (the line window's pencil and Allocate)
  4. A club book never restarts. The General ledger runs on from year to year, and the year's opening balance is worked out from it on the year's first day (3b, Ask 5). A closed year is a stretch of dates on a continuous book, so the honest place to read it is the screens that already read those dates, with the dates locked. lib/club-money-figures.ts openingBalance · plan §6 Stage 3b, Ask 5
  5. Could the reader tell which year they are reading? CLAUDE.md asks it of any surface that can show two years. Option 1 answers it on every tab: the pill carries the year's name and a lock, and a closed year carries one line under the toolbar. Option 2 answers it with the page's title, as the coach's closed season does.

Recommended: Option 1. It departs from a binding ruling, and it does so on that ruling's own reasons: the coach's ruling removes a year from thirty screens that never needed one, and a closed club year adds a lock to the three that already read a year. Nothing in the coaches portal changes. Every specimen after this screen is drawn to Option 1.

If you choose Option 2: specimens 3, 4 and 5 are redrawn as one page per closed year (its band, three shelves and the year-end report), and the Year pill's question becomes "which years may it list?".

The other seven asks are on the Decisions tab, each with its recommendation. Asks 2 to 5 shape the year itself (what closing checks, Reopen, what carries, where the year is set); Asks 6 and 7 are the two windows the owner sent to 3c from the §271 walk; Ask 8 holds what the verification found that the plan's list missed.

Stage 3c · specimen 3 of 8 · whole screen, desktop and phone · drawn to Asks 1, 2 and 3

Closing a year: one question that says what it locks, what carries and what is still open

2025–26 ended on August 31. Northfield's annual meeting is on October 20, and Priya wants the year's figures to stop moving before she prints them. Today nothing closes a year, and a line can be dated into any year at all, so the board report she prints this week can differ from the one the board reads. The proposal: a door on the Overview once a year has ended, one question window that warns and never blocks, and a closed year read where it already is, through the Year pill, with every write absent and a backdated line refused in words.

The close question, redrawn: the outcome first, then one line for each thing still open

Walking §283 walk 5 at true size, the owner liked what the question says and found it hard to read: “there seems to be a lot of text, is there a way to make this more visually appealing and easier to read and organize?” The build follows the round-1 drawing exactly, so the drawing is what changes. Everything it says stays. What moves is the order and the weight: the figure a treasurer is deciding on comes first, each thing still open takes one line, and nothing is said twice. Ask 10 · ruled 2026-10-08

Which question should 2025–26 ask?

Ruled: A, in the wide window. Owner: “I like option A but if you could make it a bit wider I think it would help this section look less jumbled and squished.” Built the same day at the kit’s wide size (800 px). The checks are walk 12 on the QA tab.

A, as recommended. It fixes what made round 1 hard to read, which is that every part carried the same weight, and not only the length. The decision becomes a figure you can find at a glance and four lines you can scan. B is quicker to build and still puts the answer last.

Either way, the rules don’t change. Closing still warns and never blocks (Ask 2), the next year still opens on the closing, locked (Ask 4), and each open row is still a door. Only the window is redrawn: no figure, route or permission moves.

For the walk: walk 5's steps 2 to 7 read this window's words. Pressing Not yet now and walking 8 to 11 while the redraw is built lets walk 5 run once, on the new window, with 6 and 7 after it. If you close now instead, seeing the new window means reopening 2025–26 a second time.

Ask 11 · ruled 2026-10-08

How should New allocation pick its teams?

Ruled: every recommendation. Owner: “I agree with your recommendations, go ahead.” Built the same day: A (group headings with a group figure), the reason beside the button in every club money window, the teams with no season on one line under the list, age order, the bill on the button, the season beside the name, and Due only for a team on its own schedule. One change from the drawing: on a phone the button reads “Bill 7 teams” and the group bands carry only their figure, since the closing band already says the total. The checks are walk 14 on the QA tab.

1 · Where the reason shows when Create is refused. Recommended: beside the button, in every club money window. The reason appears where the eye already is, and the window never jumps. It is one shared part, so all ten windows change together. The other choices are to scroll up to it (left, above) or to change only this window.

2 · Picking teams. Recommended: A, group headings with a group figure, which answers “40% to one group and 60% to another and update manually after” in one window. B (headings that only tick) does the 60/40 as two bills. C (a chooser) picks one group at a time. With A or B, a club with no groups sees a flat list with All · None.

3 · Teams with no season. Recommended: one line under the list that opens to name them. The other choice is to keep them in the list, last in their group, dimmed.

4 · Each of these can be dropped on its own: the bill on the button (“Bill 7 teams · $1,500.00”); the season beside the name instead of its own column; Due only for a team paying on its own schedule. Age order is a fix, not a choice.

What doesn’t change, whichever you pick: a create still asks; the server still splits and is the one that writes; the group is never stored on the bill (a bill is one share per team, so a team that joins Junior later isn’t added to an old bill); a team with no season still can’t be billed; one form for both doors.

For the build: the team list needs each team’s group and the club’s group order from the server, a read only, with nothing new stored. The window is being changed right now for walk 8’s fix (a team’s own payments follow its share). That fix is built but not committed, so this round is built on top of it. Walk 9 and walk 13 open this window, so the walks that follow are rewritten to match whichever option is ruled.

Stage 3c · specimen 8 of 8 · Coaches Portal, phone, true size · Ask 8b

The coach's side: the club's year never shows, and one bill must not disappear

Almost nothing in 3c reaches Aisha Rahman, 11U AA's head coach. The club's year-end never touches a team's own book, its season or any portal screen; a bill still reaches her named in the club's own words; the year's name never appears in the portal. One thing does reach her, and the verification found it: a club bill made on a season that then rolls over leaves her Club tab while it is still owed. It happens today; a September year makes it the ordinary case, because the club bills next year's costs in the fall, on the season that is ending. Drawn as a question for you, not as decided: it changes a coach screen.

What the code does

  • The Club tab reads the bills on the team's working season, both halves: it says so in its own comment.
  • The closed-season page's money shelf shows the statement's categories, not bills, so the unpaid installment is not there either.
  • The Money Overview's "Club bills due" lane and the Ledger's club schedule read every season, so they still list it, and their door opens the Club tab at a bill it no longer lists.
  • The coach can still say "We've sent it" (the write checks the team, not the season), but only from a screen that no longer shows the bill.
  • The club sees it everywhere (Allocations, Coming due, the team's account), and its roll warned about it once, when it started the 2027 season.

What else in 3c reaches the coach: nothing

  • The club's year and its name never show in the portal. A bill is named by the club ("Club insurance 2026–27" is the club's own words) and binds to the team's season, as today.
  • Closing the club's year locks the club's own books only. A team's own book is the coaches': it follows the team's season, and a coach's write is never refused because of the club's year.
  • New allocation offers only a team's open season, so a coach is never billed on a closed season again (S3C-09).
  • The year-end papers leave each team's cash out (specimen 5): it is read at load, never stored, and never stated as at the club's year-end.
  • The season doors stay the club's (Stage 2), unchanged: the roll still warns about money owed to the club, and never blocks.
Stage 3c · formatting check · done before you see the drawings

Stage 3c, checked against the Coaches Portal

Every 3c "after" frame was checked against the portal's written rules before this page was published: the table and list standard and its register, the portal kit, the design log's rulings (every one since 3b was drawn is listed below), and the screens as built, read in their code (the Budget, Budget vs. Actual, the Overview, the payee window and page, New allocation and the coach's Club tab). Three things the check found are put to you rather than settled here.

The rulings, and where each landed

RulingWhat it saysStage 3c
A record reads first, edits wholeA record opens to read; one head pencil turns all of it into its form; ✓ in the same spot turns it back; actions work in both modes.The club's year window. The payee window (option A), which today opens into an editable name. A closed year's budget line reads with no pencil. New allocation is a create, so it is the form from the start.
Edit autosaves, create asksEditing saves as you go with the floating pill; only a create gets a button.Create allocation; the year's name and the payee's name save as you go. Three things ask because they reshape or lock something: the first month (a question inside the record, as the practice library's save-over asks), Close, and Reopen (with a reason).
The olive pill chooses what is read (2026-10-07)Scope and arrangement are olive; a narrowing is quiet until it narrows.The Year pill stays the olive scope, with two glyphs in its menu (a lock, a dot), never words, so the §271 bare rows hold. Compare is drawn as built, in the plain face.
A money tab's figures above its toolbar (2026-10-07)The band first, then the toolbar; not the Overview, a document headed by its toolbar.Budget and Budget vs. Actual keep it. The Overview's ended-year line and its "From 2025–26" section sit under the toolbar, as its other sections do.
A close × is a plain glyph (2026-10-07)No outline, circle or square.Every window and sheet drawn here.
Phone sheets: a form covers the bar (2026-10-05)A form is the whole screen with a title and a 44px ×; a menu sits on top of the bar.The year window, the close question and New allocation are forms; their answers sit in the sheet's foot. The payee window is a record sheet.
Budget and Budget vs. Actual read like the coach's, six named differences (2026-10-06)A seventh difference is drift unless it is named."Against last year" on Compare is a seventh. The coach compares seasons on the closed-season page and must not gain a year on a live screen (CLAUDE.md). Put to you as Ask 8c rather than drawn as settled.
A team's cash is read, labelled, never added in (2026-10-06)Its own column, a blank in the closing row, its own band.Unchanged on the open year's board report. The year-end report leaves it out and says why in one line (specimen 5).
The coach is told what the club reads, in one quiet line (2026-10-06)One standing line at the foot of Money › Club.Unchanged. The club's year and its close never reach the portal's words.
A waiting count is the amber pillNever words added to a name.The "From 2025–26, still open" request row.
Export is one buttonNo chevron; Excel first; a 44px icon on a phone.The year-end report rides the Overview's one Export. The payee window's Export is dropped (Ask 7).
One toolbar, rare tools behind ToolsRare tools sit in the toolbar's Tools menu.The club's year is a Tools row on the Budget (the prompt's "Accounting › Tools" doesn't exist: the frame has no toolbar).
A door is olive text; an action that opens a window is an outlined button (2026-10-01)"Set the club's year" on the empty plan is a door. Close 2025–26 and Reopen open windows, so they are outlined buttons.
One control height (34px on a computer)The two small row buttons (Close, Reopen) are drawn at 34.
Required marked, never optionalA plain asterisk; no "(optional)".New allocation loses its three "(optional)" tags and its Title Case labels.

Put to you, not settled here

  • A seventh difference (Ask 8c): Compare › Against last year on the club's Budget vs. Actual only.
  • A form table, shared (Ask 6): New allocation's teams are a table whose cells hold the form's fields (a tick, and a Share input under By amount). The standard's "no controls in a cell" is written for tables that display records; no rule names a table that is a form. Tagged shared: the tournament redesign draws entry forms too.
  • A coach screen change (Ask 8b): an unpaid bill on an earlier season stays on the Club tab. Drawn on specimen 8 for you to rule.

Drift found outside 3c (recorded, not fixed)

  • Start from last year's plan copies a one-month line's stored label unchanged ("September 2026") while moving its date a year on. The screens show the date, so it shows only where a period has no date; the build fixes the label with the year work.
  • Two year readings use UTC timestamps (the payee page's first year, Allocations' "This year"); both go through the one definition in the build (S3C-01).
  • The "more than a year ahead" refusal on an entry or a transfer reads the server's calendar, not the club's day. Not 3c's; recorded.
  • D8a (the club's Payees as a window over its Ledger, like the coach's) is still the owner's call, undrawn; option A here works with Payees as a page or as a window.
Stage 3c · not drawn · listed so the build carries it

What Stage 3c builds that has no screen

None of these needs a drawing; every one has to be done before the 3c walks can pass. Ratified 2026-10-07; the build runs as two sessions, CLUB_TIER_STAGE3C_SERVER_PROMPT.md, then CLUB_TIER_STAGE3C_SCREENS_PROMPT.md.

  1. The migrations, each with the data dictionary and both snapshots in the same change. The club's year: its first month, and a row per year with its name, first and last day, and its close (who, when, the closing balance) and reopenings (who, when, why). A year can't stay a four-digit number: a change of first month makes two years share one, so the plan's lines need a key that survives it . No archive stamp on a book (Ask 8a). No close date on a season: no specimen reads one.
  2. The year's span moved, and every by-hand reading routed through it. The three definitions (the span, the year a day falls in, the year an allocation counts in) take the first month; the nine screens that work the year out by hand, the setup checklist, the payee report's "active teams", the club's quarters and the two UTC readings all ask the one definition . The one-definition guard learns to refuse a new by-hand reading.
  3. The lock, on the server. A write dated into a closed year is refused before it is made, on every club-owned book (the club's, a tournament's, the house league's), by every route that writes a line: an entry, a transfer, a receipt, an approval, a plan line or its dates, and an allocation from a closed year's line. Undo, Reverse and Void on a closed year's line are refused with the words drawn; a pending line from a closed year clears on the day it clears . A team's own book is never refused for the club's year.
  4. Close and Reopen, each one step in the database: the close checks the year has ended, records the closing balance it locked, and is refused if the year is already closed; Reopen only on the latest closed year, with its reason. Both re-checked after the write, as 3a's moves are.
  5. New allocation's server: a closed season is refused ; the line's year and the year's lock checked; the pasted ledger-entry id leaves the form (old rows keep theirs). The teams' list returns open seasons only, with the reason a team has none.
  6. The arithmetic gate re-proved across a year that starts in September, including a short year and the closed-year figures (the opening equals last year's locked closing; a closed year's Statement can't move), and the fixture rebuilt with a September year (owner's go before the reset).
  7. The old look's retirement in every file 3c rebuilds: the New allocation page (Rep Teams stylesheet, inline overrides, its own money formatter, the hand-built step bar), the payee report page if Ask 7 is A, and the payee window's always-editing form. npm run check:old-look:report lists what is left; each drop locked with --init in the same change.
  8. Help (/docs): the club's year, closing and reopening, the year-end report, New allocation from a line and from Allocations, a payee's window, and the coach's Club tab if Ask 8b is yes.
  9. Notifications: none recommended. Closing a year is the club's own act; nothing in it is news to a coach.
  10. Walks §G on the ledger, written as checkable walks on this hub's QA tab, one purpose each. The New allocation walk makes one from a budget line and reads it back: §271's W2 passed by ruling because no create was ever seen in a browser.

Recorded here, decided elsewhere

  • Stage 7: archiving a finished tournament's book, the one kind of book that ends (Ask 8a), with tournament money reaching the books.
  • /marketing: every sentence tagged on the specimens: the year window's consequences, the close question, the refusals, Reopen, the year-end report, the payee window's shortened note, the coach's band and caption (Ask 8b).
  • /docs: the help pass above.
  • Not 3c's: fiscal periods and closing entries (D2: not in the first release), bank reconciliation (its own project, both portals), tournament fees (Stage 7), families' money (Stage 5).
Stage 3d · read first · the code on 2026-10-08, after Ask 11 was committed

Where the last two money pages stand, and every door into them

You asked on 2026-10-08 whether 3c was meant to move Payees and allocations "away from pages and into drawers like how we manage similar pages in other areas of the portal". It wasn't (3c moved only New allocation and the payee's report), so 3d was added. Two club money screens are still pages: the Payees list, reached from Ledger › Tools, and an allocation, reached from five places by the plan's count. The code has ten. This screen lists them, the old addresses that must keep working, and six things this pass found that the plan's list missed. A team's account stays a page (Ask 6). What an allocation shows, and what can change

PartShown todayCan it change after it is made?
Its nameThe page's titleA route exists (a Rep Teams address kept from 3a) and no screen calls it.
The club's noteNowhereWritten once by New allocation ("for the club's own reference"), read by nothing, changed by nothing.
The line it bills from, and its year"budget line Diamond permits — city fields" in the toolbar line; the year nowhere on the pageNo. The year follows the line (or the first due date) and locks with it.
Each team's share and scheduleThe teams table, then each team's billNo writer. The read's own note says the terms "may change" on an open year, and the database locks them on a closed one, so the lock guards an edit nobody can make.
PaymentsIn each team's billYes, and these are actions, not edits: Record received, Confirm received, Undo (with a reason), Remind. A closed year's received payment shows the locked sentence instead of Undo.
Send remindersOn the allocation's toolbarIt opens the club's whole wave (every team, every bill), the same as the Allocations tab's.
ExportOn the allocation's toolbarA row per installment, with the team and each payment's method, reference and who recorded it. 3a ruled the build must not drop it. The Allocations tab's own Export is a row per allocation.

Old addresses that must keep working

  • Payees (accounting/payees, and ?payee=), and the report page 3c retired (accounting/payees/{payee}), which forwards there today.
  • An allocation (accounting/allocations/{allocation}, with or without ?bill=), and the Rep Teams address 3a moved (rep-teams/allocations/{allocation}), which forwards there today. Notices already in people's bells carry these addresses.
  • New allocation's old addresses (allocations/new, with or without ?line=) are 3c's and are unchanged.

What a head coach sees differently: nothing. Every door above is on the club's side. The coach's Money › Club tab and its bill room are not touched by 3d.

Stage 3d · specimen 4 of 4 · every door into an allocation · Asks 5 and 6

An allocation opens where you are, and closing it puts you back there

Ten doors lead into an allocation (the status screen lists them). Each could open the window over whatever it was pressed on, or move the treasurer to Allocations with the window open. The 3c walk answered this once already, for New allocation: “why do we have to leave the modal to allocate…”, and the line's window now turns into the form and comes back to the line. One rule for every door, recommended:

On this screen:

From a page (Allocations, Coming due, the Overview, Budget vs. Actual, a team's account): the allocation's window opens over that page, and × puts you back on it, where you were.

From a window (a budget line, a Ledger line, “behind the figure”): that window turns into the allocation's, the way Allocate turns a line into New allocation, and × turns it back.

From outside (the bell, an email, a bookmark, an old link): the allocation's address, which is Allocations with its window open, at the team's bill when the notice was about one.

Ask 6 · A team's account stays a page

A team's account gathers one team's bills, requests and history across its seasons, under a season band each. It is a view of many records, which the portal makes a page (or a tab), not a record you read and edit, so it stays a page with its back arrow, as the plan recommended. Only its doors change: a billed or received row opens the team's bill over the account page, per the rule above, and a request row keeps opening Payment requests with that request's window (unchanged). The bill's own “Open {team}’s account” stays a page link: from inside a window it moves to the page, which is where an account lives.

Stage 3d · not drawn · listed so the build carries it

What Stage 3d builds that has no screen

None of these needs a drawing; every one has to be done before the 3d walks can pass. Ratified 2026-10-08, every ask as recommended (owner: “I agree with your recommendations”); the build runs as one session from CLUB_TIER_STAGE3D_BUILD_PROMPT.md.

  1. The window kit learns two things. A named back for a level inside a window (“← Payees”, “← Diamond fees 2026”): shown at a desk, the bare ← on a phone, and the phone's Back goes there first (the kit's dialog floor already has the hook the coach's room uses). And, if Ask 7a is yes, a form that stands over another form, on its own layer between the form layer and the question layer.
  2. One allocation window, opened by every host. It reads its allocation by id, holds both levels (the allocation, a team's bill) and their questions (Record, Confirm, Undo, Remind), and tells the screen under it when money moved, so that screen re-reads its own figures: Allocations and Coming due, the Budget line, the Ledger line, Budget vs. Actual, the Overview, a team's account.
  3. The allocation's read and one write. The read adds the club's note (S3D-03). One edit route, under Accounting, takes the name and the note, refuses a blank name and a closed year's bill in words (the year lock's own refusal), and checks the member's team groups; the Rep Teams route kept from 3a retires. The terms (shares, schedule, teams) stay unwritable (Ask 7b).
  4. Send reminders leaves the allocation (S3D-04); the Allocations tab and each team's bill keep theirs.
  5. One joined band for every club money summary. The allocation's figures and its bill's open on the portal's money band (one frame, a hairline between figures, two-up on a phone), not separate cards; the club money kit's separate-card parts retire, a team's account joining the band too (recommended, no drawing needed).
  6. The Payees window replaces the page: Ledger › Tools opens it; the payee window (§283 W10) becomes its second level with Previous · Next; Delete moves to the end of the body; Merge and New payee ask as today.
  7. Every old address forwards in one hop (the table on specimen 4): Payees and ?payee= to the Ledger with the window; the retired report page straight there; an allocation's page and the Rep Teams one to Allocations with the window, keeping ?bill=. Notices already in people's bells keep working through these forwards.
  8. Notices write the new address, and the bell's label reader, which today names a notice “Open the bill” or “Open the allocation” from the page's address, learns it (its unit test pins both).
  9. The gates. The two retired pages' old look leaves (check:old-look, locked in the same change); the export catalog, which names the allocation page as its Export's home, follows the window (check:export-catalog); the layout sweep's three screens that point at the retired pages are repointed to the windows (and gain the phone); the UAT notices seed writes the new address; the 3c screens guard's Payees path and the payee tests follow the window.
  10. Help (/docs): Payees (from Tools and from the picker), an allocation (what it reads, the name and the note, a closed year's), a team's bill inside it, and where each door now opens.
  11. Walks, a new ledger section, checkable on this hub's QA tab, one purpose each: Payees from Tools; Payees from inside Add entry with the typing kept; merging Mizuno Canada Ltd. into Mizuno Canada (a write, read back on the Ledger); an allocation from every door, each closing back where it started; renaming one and reading the coach's Club tab; a closed year's allocation; and the phone for each.

  • /marketing: the name's hint, the closed year's line for a bill, and the help words.
  • /docs: the help pass above.

Stage 6 · read from the code on 2026-10-08, before anything was drawn

Where the venues stand: three books, two clash checks, one program with none

Stage 6 draws four things, in this order of value: one venue book, one clash check across every program, the club calendar, and the Venue library fixed and redrawn. Every sentence on this screen was re-read in the code today. Four places where the plan’s §4D was out of date are corrected below, and the counts are in the notes. One correction changes the shape of the stage. The prompt counted clashes between programs: rep × league, rep × tournament and league × tournament. But the club the first release is for is a rep club with no house league, and its most likely double-booking is two of its own teams on one diamond. That is rep × rep, so it is counted too, and the check covers it.

On this screen:

The three venue books, as the code holds them today

The club’s Venue library

  • Venues, each with its facilities (diamonds, fields, courts, rinks…), one list per club. League, Club and Club · Association plans.
  • House league points at it directly: a league game or practice holds the venue and the facility it was given.
  • Saving needs the tournament permission, so only the owner and an admin can save; a league admin cannot (D02).
  • Delete is final, with no in-use check, and every house-league game on that venue silently loses it (S6-08).

A tournament’s own copy

  • “Import from Library” copies a venue and its facilities into the tournament and stamps where it came from.
  • Nothing ever reads that stamp. A clone drops it, “import from a past tournament” drops it, and importing twice makes two copies.
  • The setup wizard’s venue search offers other tournaments’ copies, never the library (a Tournament Stage 5 finding, recorded there).

Each team’s place book (Coaches Portal)

  • Built 2026-09-21: up to 100 places per team, each with an address, a usual diamond and a note, reached by typing in Location.
  • An event keeps its own copy of name, address and diamond, plus a link to the place.
  • The diamond is free text (“Diamond 2”). Nothing links a place or an event to a club venue, and Arrival & Places ruled that on purpose (“the admin’s library stays admin’s”). Ask 1 reverses that for club teams.

Every clash check today

The one shared piece is the “same surface?” answer both engines use. It is module-agnostic, but a league id and a tournament id come from different tables, so they can never match. Typed words never match a picked diamond. The clock: tournaments store a local date and time, while league and rep events store instants. The cross-program check compares instants and turns a tournament game into one with the conversion the live-score code already uses.

Dev has no clash to count, because no club has a venue to clash on. The case therefore rests on three things. The club’s first season, when its teams share three or four diamonds. The demo’s weekly double-booking, which the seed writes and nothing has ever flagged. And the release target itself, a rep club whose clashes are between its own teams. ⚠ The test club (“UAT Rep Club”) has no venues, no places and no event on a venue: the walks need venues seeded as an additive step, never a reset.

Corrections to the plan’s §4D (re-read today)

  • D03: the per-program admin schedule it cites is gone. The admin’s read-only team schedule already files days in the platform’s zone. The device clock survives in three week/month groupings: the coach schedule, the house-league admin schedule, and the public league schedule. The public one groups by the server’s clock, which is UTC on the host, so a Sunday game after 8 p.m. can file into next week (S6-12).
  • D05: the old sidebar it cites no longer exists. The doors today are the rail (“Venue library”, Organization group), the house-league schedule’s “Set up your diamonds once”, and a “Venues” tile on the Organization page with no plan gate (S6-11).
  • D07: the calendar export’s “STUB” header was already trued on 2026-09-25. The team-wide feed is still dead: nothing ever makes its link. The help article still promises a subscribable link “in a future release”.
  • Time: there is no per-club time zone. Every org runs on one platform setting, Eastern (Toronto). “The club’s zone” means that setting today.

Today nothing on the form can know that: her “Lions Park” is a row in her team’s own place book, its diamond is the words “Diamond 2”, and 14U AA’s is another team’s words. This reverses a ruling. Arrival & Places (2026-09-21, §5 “Not built, on purpose”) kept the club’s venue library away from coaches: “admin’s org_venues stays admin’s”. Its reason was a coach’s own convenience: a book the coach owns, with nothing to wait for from the club. That reason still holds for a team outside a club, and for every place a club doesn’t own. It does not answer a clash between two of the club’s own teams, which a team’s private book can never see. So Ask 1 is asked as its own question. venues drawn, not seeded

What picking each does

  • The club’s Lions Park: the event keeps a link to the club’s venue and copies its name and address, the way a place does today, so the family calendar and the Maps link work unchanged. A Diamond list appears beside Venue (Ask 2). The clash check runs.
  • The team’s own Lions Park: exactly as built. The diamond stays free text in More, and the event is not compared with anyone (Ask 3: a typed place never clashes, and the form says so).
  • Typing anything else: saves as plain words, as today.

Where the link lives (build note): on the event, the venue and the diamond, the same two links a house-league game holds. The plan’s line said “a place references a venue”. But a place can’t carry the diamond, which changes game by game, and the check needs both.

Stage 6 · specimen 2 · the rule every program’s line is drawn from · Asks 3 and 4

What counts as a clash, in one clock, and where a program’s own refusal stays

One rule, written before any line is drawn, so the build can put it in one place and test it once. The writers on the previous screen all call it. Then the harder question: house league and tournaments already refuse some of their own double-bookings. Stage 6 proposes that every new comparison only warns. So two rules will sit side by side on the same diamond, and this screen says so plainly rather than leaving it to be found.

On this screen:
RecommendedThe rule

Same venue, same facility, overlapping time

Ask 3
CaseWhat the line saysWhy
Same venue, same facility, the times overlap“Diamond 2 is booked by 14U AA practice, 5:30–7:30 p.m.”The only exact case. Overlap means one starts before the other ends: a 6:00 end and a 6:00 start do not clash.
Same venue, the facility not set on one sideSofter: “Lions Park is busy then: … Pick a diamond to be sure.”It may be another diamond. The line asks for the one fact that settles it.
A place that isn’t the club’s (a team’s own place, typed words)Never compared. In a club with a library: “Not one of the club’s venues, so it isn’t checked for clashes.”Words can’t be trusted to mean the same diamond (house league already treats typed words as a weak warning, and a picked diamond never matches words). Saying so in place is what keeps a coach from assuming a silent form means a free diamond.
CancelledNever clashes.As every engine does today.
PostponedA postponed league game never clashes at its old time; it clashes once it has a new one.As house league does today. A rep event has no postponed state: a postponement is a move, so it clashes at its new time.
A rep event with no endCounted as 90 minutes.House league and tournaments both assume 90 already. The coach’s form fills an end two hours after the start, so a missing end is a blanked field, an import, or an older event: 119 of 259 timed rep events on dev.
A tournament gameIts own length: the game’s, else its division’s, else the tournament’s, else 90 minutes.The tournament’s own chain, read once. Its buffer stays inside the tournament: across programs, only real overlap counts.
A team’s copy of its own tournament gameNever compared with that game.The tournament writes its games into each linked team’s schedule. Without this rule, every game a club team plays in the club’s own tournament would clash with itself.
A team against itselfNo line.Two of a team’s own bookings at once is a schedule mistake, not a diamond question (the coach sees both on the schedule).
An outside tournament (dates only)Never compared.It holds no venue and no time of day.

The word

The rule is the same for every sport: a venue and one of its facilities. What a line or a label says is the sport’s own word, read from the team’s, the league season’s or the tournament’s sport: “Diamond 2 is booked by …” and “Pick a diamond to be sure” for softball and baseball, “Court 2 …” and “Pick a court” for basketball, “Field” when a sport has none. Nothing on a Stage 6 screen writes the word in: it is the switch the schedule forms and house league’s “Set up your diamonds once” already read (owner, 2026-10-08). These drawings show a softball club, so they say diamond.

The clock

Every booking is compared as a moment in time. House-league and rep events are stored that way already. A tournament game’s date and time are read in the platform’s zone (Eastern, Toronto), daylight saving included, with the same conversion the live-score screens use. ⚠ There is no per-club zone: a club outside Eastern time would compare correctly with itself, but every time it is shown would be Eastern (Ask 7).

RecommendedRefuse or warn, by pair

Each program keeps its own refusal; everything that crosses a boundary warns

Ask 4
The two bookingsTodayProposed
Two house-league games or practicesRefused, on the server, after CreateStill refused. Only where it says so moves: under the Diamond field, before Create (specimen 3).
Two games in one tournamentRefused in the Add/Edit window and the inline edit, in the browser onlyStill refused there, unchanged. Why four tournament writers skip it is Tournament Stage 3’s question (S6-03): not this stage’s to settle.
Two of the club’s tournaments on one weekendNothingWarns
Two club teams (rep × rep)NothingWarns: no team can refuse another team’s booking; the club decides
A club team and a house-league bookingNothingWarns, on both forms
A club team and a club tournament gameNothingWarns, on both forms
A house-league booking and a club tournament gameNothingWarns, on both forms

Said plainly: on Kinsmen Park, Diamond B, Tuesday at 6:00 p.m., the league admin who books a second league game there is refused. If the diamond is held by 11U AA’s practice instead, the same game saves with an amber line. That is deliberate. A double-booked league diamond is the league’s own mistake, which the league can always fix. A diamond shared with another program is a question between two people with equal claims, and a form refusing one of them would hand one volunteer a veto over another’s schedule. The club calendar is where the club sees both and settles it.

Not recommended, drawn as the alternatives: (b) refuse every exact clash everywhere. It is the tidiest rule, but it makes a coach’s practice depend on whether the house league saved first, and on the day the club has permits the refusal would be wrong half the time. (c) Warn everywhere, retiring house league’s refusal: a change to a working rule this stage has no evidence for.

Ask 7 · timeAsk 8 · the device-clock leftovers

One clock on the calendar from day one, and three older screens fixed beside it

  • The calendar files every day in the platform’s one zone (Eastern, Toronto), and says so once: “Times in Eastern time.” A club outside Eastern time would read Eastern times. No org records a zone or a province today, so the count of orgs it would affect can’t be read: dev holds 8 tournaments marked ON and 19 unmarked, and the production read waits for your go. Recommended: a platform item, ahead of the first club outside Eastern time (the zone module already plans it as one setting per org, passed through the helpers every caller already uses). Not this stage’s to build.
  • Ask 8, recommended: one small fix that rides 6b, so the club’s three week and month groupings agree with the calendar. Today they group by the device’s clock: the coach’s schedule weeks and months, and the house-league admin schedule’s weeks. The public league schedule groups by the server’s clock (UTC on the host), so a Sunday game after 8 p.m. files into the next week . The admin’s team schedule is already right and is drawn unchanged.
Stage 6 · specimen 6 · the club admin · Organization › Venue library, true size (960 today, 1200 proposed) · Ask 9

The Venue library saves for the people who schedule, and says what each venue holds

Once the coach’s picker reads it, the library is the club’s one venue book, and it has to hold up to that. Today saving needs the tournament permission, so only the owner and an admin can save. The league admin, whom house league sends here, is refused. A failed load reads as an empty library. Delete is final and checks nothing, and every house-league game on that venue silently loses it. A facility can’t be renamed, though the server allows it. And the copy names only tournaments. It is also one of the two club areas still wearing the old look, which its build retires. venues drawn, not seeded

Every writer runs the check, each with a test

  • Rep teams: add one event; add a weekly series (every date); edit, move or un-cancel one event; edit a series (this and future, all); the schedule file import (a warning per row); the place book’s “Also update the upcoming events” (a summary of what landed on a club booking). The tournament mirror is skipped and tested as skipped: it must never compare a team’s copy of a game with the game.
  • House league: add and edit a game; add a practice (single and series); the season generator (counted in its existing after-save summary). Each keeps its own refusal against league bookings and adds the cross-program warning.
  • Tournaments: add and edit a game; drag on the timeline; the pool-play generator; playoffs; the rain-delay shift (a database function today, which needs its own call after it runs); field lanes resolved; the schedule import. Each returns the cross-program warnings. None changes the tournament’s own rule.
  • One rule, one place: the comparison lives beside the existing “same surface?” answer, and one list of cases (the rule screen’s table) is its unit test. A guard test fails if a new writer of an event’s time or place appears without calling it.
  • The permit hook: the check returns findings with a kind (“booked by”, “busy then”), so Stage 10 adds “outside the club’s permit” without changing a caller.

The data the build adds (with its dictionary lines and snapshot refresh; production order recorded)

  • An event’s club venue and diamond: two optional links on a rep event, the same two a house-league game holds. This replaces the plan’s “a place references a venue”, because the facility changes game by game.
  • Archive: the venue table’s existing “active” column, used at last, and a facility’s equivalent if a facility can archive.
  • The tournament copy’s link: kept by a clone and by import-from-past, plus the missing index on the facility copy’s link.
  • The database rule: members read venues, and only the server writes them.
  • Indexes for the clash lookup: rep events by club and start time.

How to read this: the colour is the worst thing a club hits in that area today, verified in the code on 2026-09-25 and cross-checked against the June audit. Click a chip or a flag to read what the code does and what the plan does about it.
Product-manager brief

Club Tier Production Readiness

What it is

A staged programme that takes the Club plan from "built but never tested" to "a rep club can buy it, set it up, staff it, run a season on it and trust the numbers it shows the board." Each part of the offer is tackled, walked and signed off one at a time, in the order a real club meets them. House league is deliberately last so Club can be released to rep clubs that run no house league.

Why it matters

  • Club is the top of the pricing ladder and has never been validated against one real club. Every June pricing decision is still a hypothesis.
  • The club-admin side has been effectively static since June while the Coaches Portal got three months of intensive work. The two halves now disagree about money, seasons, venues and who can do what.
  • The June audit of the club president's journey found the oversight layer "part broken and part unguarded". Today's re-verification: of its 50 findings, 7 fixed, 6 partly, 4 superseded, 33 still open. Of the 27 staff-admin findings, 19 still open.
  • Every coach in a club is on a free Premium portal until September 2027. A club pays $219 a month only for what the club side gives it. That is exactly the side that has never been QA'd.

What the club sees and does differently when this is done

Buying and setting up. A club owner is provisioned (or buys) onto Club or Club · Association, sees the right price and trial, is walked through a club-shaped setup, and lands on a hub that leads with the club's own programs. Cancelling and coming back restores everything.

Staffing the board. The owner invites an admin who can see the club's modules, a treasurer and a registrar, from the Members screen, with roles that mean what the screen says. A volunteer who also coaches elsewhere can be invited.

Teams and coaches. The owner creates teams and program years, names coaches, and each coach lands in a populated Premium portal at no per-team charge. Starting and closing a season means the same thing on both sides. The president gets one oversight view of every team.

Money the board can repeat. The treasurer plans a budget for the club's year, allocates to teams, approves coach requests with a confirmation and a way back, and reads one board summary whose every figure is true by construction and guarded by a build check. Team money and club money are two clearly separated things; the club reads the coach's records rather than keeping a shadow copy.

A public face that leads with the rep program. Families find the teams, open tryouts and the club's colours. "Tryouts are open" takes them to the tryout. Unlisting from the directory no longer takes down the website.

Families. Household records read the same money the Money hub does, a changed guardian email follows the child, a merge stays merged, and the export says what it holds.

One venue book. Rep, house-league and tournament games read the same venues, and a diamond double-booked across modules is flagged.

The club’s schedules (added and ruled 2026-10-08). A scheduler for the club’s shared time: parameters in, a draft out, adjusted by hand, finalized, kept by name, summarized and sent to the people who need it. Drawn with permits; the first release waits for it; League Plus and both Club bands carry it alike.

Tested and documented. A Club fixture and browser suite, admin screens in the layout sweep, help that describes today's screens, marketing that promises only what exists.

Who benefits

Club owners and presidents (the buyer), treasurers, registrars and admins (the roles the plan sells but the screen cannot assign today), coaches in a club (their portal stays; the club side stops contradicting it), and families. Standalone Premium coaches are unaffected.

Trade-offs

  • Fix the club side to read the coach's records rather than rebuilding both money models — the coach side has three months of hardening and build gates; the club's copy has neither.
  • Permits and a club-wide calendar are new features, not readiness items. Both are decided: the club calendar is in the first release (D5), and permits are Stage 10, which the release waits for (D4, amended 2026-09-25). Because Stage 10 sits on Stage 6’s venue book and clash check, the release waits for Stage 6 too. The risk left is size, not a decision.
  • Families P3 is not release-gating; its four serious defects are.
  • House league last, and no new plan needs inventing — League Plus already is the standalone plan.

Success criteria

  1. One real rep club (or the fixture standing in) completes the nine-point exit definition with the owner watching; every stage's QA walk is on the ledger as passed.
  2. Every board-facing figure has a build gate, and the same number cannot be computed two ways on two screens.
  3. Every June audit finding routed to Club is fixed or explicitly superseded — none open.
  4. Club and Club · Association can be bought in-product, the gate flip is one decision away, and the marketing surfaces promise only what exists.
Full plan — condensed

Ten stages, one exit definition

The full ledger lives in the plan file

CLUB_TIER_PRODUCTION_READINESS_PLAN.md carries every finding with its code anchor (sections 4A–4I), the eleven rulings (§5), sequencing (§7), build gates (§8), the release checklist (§9) and the June-audit register (§11). This tab is the reading version.

Release-ready for a rep club means

  1. Buy or be provisioned onto Club with the right price, trial and comp state; cancel and come back with everything restored.
  2. Staff the board — owner, an admin who sees the modules, a treasurer, a registrar — including volunteers who coach elsewhere.
  3. Create teams and program years, name coaches, every coach lands in a populated Premium portal; a season starts and closes the same way on both sides.
  4. Plan a budget for a club year, allocate, receive requests, mark money received, and read one board summary that is true by construction and guarded.
  5. Show a public face that leads with the rep program.
  6. Know its families — same money as the Money hub, merges that hold, emails that follow the child.
  7. Keep one venue book every module reads.
  8. Coexist with tournaments — the club's own team enters its own event, the mirror keeps the coach's schedule true.
  9. Be tested: fixture, browser suite, layout sweep, current help, truthful marketing.
  10. Hold its permits (ruled in 2026-09-25): the club records the field, diamond or ice permits it holds, every module's scheduling reads them, and a permit's cost sits in the budget. Stage 10, and the release waits for it.

Stages

Stage 0 — Ground truth

Fixes + fixture + rulings · no mockup · walk §A

Seed the Club fixture (six teams, three program-year states, real coach memberships, guardians shared across teams, a budget year, allocations, requests, a tournament with the club's own team). Fix the dead-control class in one sweep: the two money-entry controls, the audit log, the dead rep-team links, the reminder-button roles, the tryouts card. Ship the security fix-now on its own: the house-league tenant-boundary hole, the archive org check, rate limits, escaped emails. Rule D1, D2, D8. Walk it end to end. Exit: every club screen opens for owner, admin and treasurer without a wall.

Stage 1 — The club shell

Provision · buy · cancel · return · roles · nav · settings · walk §B

Prerequisite (owner, 2026-09-25): the Admin Design Continuity foundation lands first, so every admin screen, tournament screens included, already follows the account theme in both palettes before the club shell is rebuilt on it. Mockups: a plan-aware hub (what the club runs first; a president's morning brief), the phone bar and More sheet for a club, Members with board roles and a coach row, the billing page for a Club with both band prices and a prorated move to Club · Association (D7), Org Settings that name the public-site switch honestly, the club onboarding checklist, the audit log. Roles per D8; the hub decides "tournament-only" from the plan; the membership policy stops counting coach rows; comp scoped to the promo plans; reactivate restores everything; one gating source; the coach portal checks the plan on downgrade. 1b · Buying Club and Club · Association (ruled 2026-09-25): both band prices published, a real Club purchase on the billing page, and the Club ↔ Club · Association move as a prorated subscription change rather than a second checkout; no Founding Season banner ever speaks for Club.

Stage 2 — Rep teams & the coach bridge

Rulings D10 + the club season lifecycle first · walks §C §D, Shared Book §1.16, host-own-team

An "Invite a coach" door that writes the membership and sends the mail. The club gets the same season roll the standalone portal has, invoked by the admin; whether a Draft year may run beside the Active one is Ask 1 (drawn 2026-09-28, recommending one model: tryouts on the working season). A team page with edit and a "what the club sees" panel (coach in place · roster · next event · documents · money owed — the franchise health board). Finish the ownership-transfer routine so a standalone coach's portal can join the club without losing its data, with a gate that keeps it complete. One rule for roster counts and one for records.

Stage 3 — Club money (four parts)

D1 + D2 applied · walks §E §F §G · new build gates

3a bookkeeping core and the allocation/request loop: team ledgers read-only and labelled, transfers void both sides, payees managed; allocations with true overdue and team names; confirm on every money move, a way back, one atomic write per transfer, the coach's meaning visible to the club. 3b budget with many allocations per line and next year plannable; Budget vs. Actual with actuals by line; one headroom definition; the board summary (club position · receivables · team-held money labelled · one export); Budget and Summary in the sidebar. 3c the club year: label + start month, year-end lock and carry, ledgers archived. Gates: the summary's arithmetic recomputed from rows, one definition per figure, transfer atomicity. 3a drawn 2026-09-30 (Mockups → Stage 3a): seven specimens, a re-read of every money row, five new findings and six asks, all ratified the same day as recommended (hub v22). Redrawn the same day to the coach’s Money format, with the frame posed as two options (Ask 2). 3b drawn 2026-10-05 (Mockups → Stage 3b): a re-read of every row 3b owns, each figure’s one definition, six specimens (the Budget · Budget vs. Actual · the board summary · a team’s money · the shared-payee report · the coach’s side), a formatting check and a Not-drawn list; nine asks on the Decisions tab (Ask 5, the Months view, added 2026-10-06 at the owner's question), all ratified 2026-10-06 as recommended, with the two coach month-grid fixes; build prompts CLUB_TIER_STAGE3B_SERVER_PROMPT.md then CLUB_TIER_STAGE3B_SCREENS_PROMPT.md. A /design pass the same day redrew the places the drawings had drifted from the coach's screens (listed on the Formatting check). 3b built 2026-10-06 (the server session committed 26277b5f; the screens session committed baefbe7d (the rulings) and ad957b4e (the build) the same day, after /simplify, /review, check:layout in both themes and /design at 1440 and 390): eleven walks, ledger §271, on the QA tab; a twelfth, the Ledger’s Item column (2026-10-07), is ledger §279. 3c mockup item added 2026-10-07 (the owner, in the §271 walk): New allocation, redrawn. Today Allocate leaves the line’s window for a three-step page in the old Rep Teams style, and Create lands on the allocation’s own page, so the treasurer goes back to the Budget and reopens the line by hand. Two shapes to draw: A, the line’s window turns into the allocation form on one screen and returns to the line with the new allocation listed (recommended); B, a one-screen page in the portal’s format that returns to the line. And a design review added the same day (the owner, at W10): what the teams recorded paying a shared payee opens a page of its own from the payee’s window. Recommended: it becomes the body of that window, which reads first and edits whole under one pencil (the window opens straight into an editable name today); the alternative keeps the page and opens it from the Payees list. Full item in the plan, §6 Stage 3c. 3c drawn 2026-10-07 (Mockups → Stage 3c): where the year is read today (about a dozen places, not one), Ask 1 (a closed year read in place, a departure from the coach’s one-page ruling, argued on its reasons), and eight specimens: setting the club’s year (the year that changes is the next one, short), every money page reading a named year, closing a year (warns, never blocks; a closed year locked in place; Reopen with a reason), the year that opens, the annual meeting’s papers (against last year, the year-end report), New allocation in the line’s window, the payee window reading first with its report inside, and the coach’s side (an unpaid bill must not leave the Club tab at a roll). Ratified 2026-10-07, every ask as recommended, with Ask 9: the club’s year is its fiscal year, on the club side only. The Payees list opens over the Ledger, as the coaches portal’s does, and an allocation opens as a window that reads first. A team’s account stays a page. Drawn first, after 3c’s last two walks (W12, W13). 3d drawn 2026-10-08 (Mockups → Stage 3d), after the code was read: ten doors into an allocation where the plan named five, and six findings (an entry being added is lost through the payee picker’s “Manage payees…”; nothing about an allocation can be changed after it is made; its note is shown nowhere; its Send reminders is the whole club’s; the doors; the old addresses). Four specimens: Payees over the Ledger with a payee one level in; an allocation as a window that reads the bill first and whose pencil edits only its name and note; a team’s bill one level inside it; and one rule for every door (it opens where you are, and closing puts you back). Ratified 2026-10-08, every ask as recommended, with the owner’s correction that a summary’s figures are one joined band; the build runs as one session from CLUB_TIER_STAGE3D_BUILD_PROMPT.md.

Stage 4 — The club's public face

Walk §H · marketing truth

Home for a rep-only club (programs first, tournaments last and absent when none, the club's colours, a footer with contact); a Teams index and a Teams tab; the tryout funnel; the editor with section controls; the coach's public URL with a copy button; the same public checks on every page; the archive org check. Marketing: "coming soon" out when Stage 8 says so, the false "parent notifications" and "field bookings" lines removed, README and comparison table reconciled.

Stage 5 — Families

Walks §54 + §56 · P3 mockup session after release (D9)

Merges that hold, emails that follow the child, money from the payments table, an export that says what it holds, paging for association-scale clubs, a duplicate rule that uses first names, a role floor, a send cap, Reply-To to the club, children counted once. Confirm the merge function is on production.

Stage 6 — Venues, scheduling, permits

Rulings D3 D4 D5 first · walk §I

One venue book: a coach's place can be one of the club's venues; tournaments read their source venue; a cross-module clash check warns on every write. Venue Library gates and errors fixed. An internal read-only club calendar in org time. The venue book and clash check are shaped so permits (Stage 10) can plug in. Drawn 2026-10-08 (Mockups → Stage 6, beside 3d): seven specimens and thirteen asks, ratified 2026-10-08, every one as recommended (the seventh, one way to enter where an event is on every form, asked by the owner the same day). Built as two sessions: 6a the venue book, the clash check and the one Where field (CLUB_TIER_STAGE6A_BUILD_PROMPT.md), then 6b the club calendar and the Venue library (CLUB_TIER_STAGE6B_BUILD_PROMPT.md).

Stage 7 — Tournaments in a club + one door to every family

Walk §J

The hub banner logic for a club; one-click "add my team" for a club org; tournament fees into the books by decision; one org-wide announcement door with a preview count, suppression, a send log and a cap.

Stage 8 — Release readiness

Go/no-go on the nine points

A Club browser suite on the fixture; admin club routes in the layout sweep; every club help article re-read; a demo decision; pricing and marketing drift check; the gate flip runbook and checkout verified; migrations on prod in order with functions verified; support posture and rollback runbook; the release and cohort shape logged.

Stage 9 — House league (its own release track)

Its own plan when it opens · D11 · may run alongside Stage 10

The trust-plan defects re-verified and closed; the standalone-plan coupling check; the ledger seam under D1's pattern; venues under Stage 6's book; confirms on one-click season changes; League Plus un-parked as the standalone plan.

Stage 10 — Permits & bookings (ruled in 2026-09-25; the release waits for it)

New feature · its own plan, PM brief and mockup session · walk §K

A permit is a record the club holds: venue, date range, weekly slots, cost and payee, the issuer's reference and document, and who it is for. Scheduling reads it — the clash check gains "is this slot inside a permit we hold?", the league generator and club calendar can offer permitted slots, a coach's event at a club venue shows the permit it sits in. Money reads it — a permit's cost can be cited by a budget line and allocated to teams. A per-permit view of used vs unused slots. Out of the first cut: requesting or paying for permits through the platform, municipal integrations, public booking.

Stage 11 — The club’s schedules: a scheduler (added 2026-10-08)

Added by the owner · ruled 2026-10-08 · drawn with Stage 10 in one session · the release waits for it · walk §L

A club admin hands out the club’s shared time (a dome’s winter hours, the pitching tunnel’s nights, house league’s practice slots): a few parameters in (which venue and facilities, when, which teams, how much each gets, and rules folded away until wanted), a draft out, adjusted by hand the way a tournament director adjusts a generated schedule, then finalized. Each schedule is kept by name (“Winter dome 2026–27”), reopened or copied next year, read as summaries (the whole dome, one team, one program) and sent to stakeholders (house league admins, each team’s coaches) with a preview and a send log; families see their team’s slots on its schedule. It hands out time, not game pairings. Ruled 2026-10-08: a club slot shows on a team’s schedule as “From the club”, read-only to the coach, who can hand it back (D3 amended narrowly, the tournament-game pattern); one model of the club’s time shared with permits, so Stages 10 and 11 are drawn together; owner and admin build it, a league admin for house league’s teams; time only; the release waits for it; League Plus and both Club bands carry it alike (logged with /strategy).

Sequencing

Stage 1 before everything — no other walk is honest while admins and treasurers are tournament-only users. Stage 2 before 3 — the allocation loop needs teams, program years and the season rule. Stages 4, 5, 6, 7 are independent of each other and of 3. Stage 10 needs Stage 6's venue book and Stage 3's allocations, and the release waits for it, so Stage 8's go/no-go comes after Stages 3, 6 and 10 at the earliest. Stage 9 is its own release track.

Findings referenced on the map

A01 — Anyone but the owner is a tournament-only user

Admin and staff have no module permissions by default; the hub decides "tournament-only" from the member, not the plan, and redirects them into tournaments or an owner-only setup page that bounces them back. Stage 1, ruling D8.

A02 — The board cannot be staffed from the screen

Treasurer, registrar and league admin exist in the product but not in the invite or role pickers; saving another role quietly turns it into staff; help still tells owners to pick Treasurer. Stage 1.

A03 — A coach who coaches elsewhere cannot join a club's board

The membership policy counts the plumbing rows every coaching-staff invite writes, so the invite, the acceptance and a reinstatement all refuse. Contradicts the July account-model decision. Stage 1.

A05 — No way to buy Club

The billing shelf only opens an article; only Tournament Plus can be upgraded to; Club · Association appears on no customer surface; the team-cap error tells a club to upgrade with nowhere to go. Stage 1, ruling D7.

A07 — Coming back after cancelling restores nothing

Resubscribing restores only a plan-downgrade retention; the site stays hidden, tournaments stay archived, and the retention job later emails a paying customer that their window expired. Stage 1.

A08 — The Founding Season comp leaks onto Club

Every signup gets the comp; moving the org to Club does not revoke it; the billing page then says Club is free through 2027 beside a $219 card. Stage 1, ruling D6.

A09 — "Listed on /discover" is the master switch for the whole site

The checkbox writes the public flag, which hides the org home, the league pages and every link back to the org. The real directory flag has no control. Stage 1.

B01 — A new head coach must be invited as staff or admin

No Coach role exists to invite; the Coaches page assigns only existing active members; no email tells the coach they were assigned; between seasons a coach cannot be added at all. Stage 2, ruling D10.

B03 — Club teams have no season rollover

"Start next season" is standalone-only; the club's new program year is blank; a new year is blocked while one is active, so next season's tryouts cannot open until this season is marked complete — which locks every coach out. Stage 2.

B04 — Adopting a standalone portal orphans the team

The transfer routine was written when the team had 17 tables and never revised; it leaves behind the coach's access record and roughly 48 tables added since. The customer UI calls the rest "platform-assisted". Stage 2.

B05 — The coach portal never checks the plan

A club that downgrades keeps every team's full Premium portal while the downgrade copy says it shuts down. Stage 1.

B06 — Dead doors on the club side

"View roster" and two sidebar links go to pages that do not exist; the "Ungrouped" filter crashes the team list. Stage 0.

B08 — No cross-team oversight

Team cards answer roster, pending and families only; three different roster-count rules and two record rules across the club screens. Stage 2.

C01 — Two money-entry controls dead since June

The payee box on the ledger form and add-item / add-category on the budget form call routes that now require the org and get refused. Stage 0.

C03 — A treasurer cannot finish the allocation loop

The allocate wizard loads teams from rep-teams routes the treasurer cannot see, so the team list is empty; the reminder buttons are shown to treasurers and always refused. Stage 0 / 1.

C04 — Net position mixes team and league money into the club's figure

Every ledger counts and none is ever archived; there is no whole-club picture. Stage 3, ruling D1.

C05 — Headroom is budget minus at most 50 expenses

A club with more than fifty expense entries in a year is shown a wrong headline. Stage 3.

C07 — Money moves on one click with no reversal and a race

Approve is one click, the accounting entry is never linked so nothing can be reversed, two approvals can post two transfers, and a lost race leaves an orphaned transfer. Stage 3a.

C10 — The club cannot plan next year

Only the current year and years with lines can be chosen; allocation resolves the current calendar year only; no year-end exists while the coach side has close, settlement and carry-forward. Stage 3c, ruling D2.

C18 — Tournament money never reaches the books

Fees live on the team row; house-league fee entries are created on approval day, never voided, and can be revived. Stage 7 by decision.

D01 — Double-booking checks stop at module boundaries

Each module checks only itself; rep-team events check nothing. Stage 6.

D02 — The venue library refuses the person the scheduler sends there

Saving a venue needs a tournament permission a league admin lacks, and the page swallows the refusal. Stage 6.

D03 — No club calendar

Nothing spans teams; the admin's team schedule shows device time and buckets days by UTC. Stage 6, ruling D5.

D04 — The admin cannot add a game

By the franchise ruling coaches own the schedule; admin writes were removed deliberately. Stage 6, ruling D3.

D06 — Permits do not exist

No table, route, page or plan; the homepage says clubs manage field bookings. Stage 6, ruling D4.

D05 — The Venue library’s guard, rename, copy and doors

Delete is final and checks nothing, and house league’s bookings lose the venue; no facility rename on the page; copy names tournaments and house league only; the Organization tile has no plan gate. Stage 6b, Ask 9.

D07 — The team-wide calendar feed is dead

Nothing makes its link; the export’s “STUB” header was trued 2026-09-25; help still promises a subscribable link. Ask 10: to the schedule deep dive’s stage 4.

S6-01 — The release target’s clashes are between its own teams

A rep club with no house league double-books between its own teams; the check covers rep × rep. Ask 3.

S6-02 — The coach demo double-books its own diamond every week

Every home game and practice of the demo’s teams is seeded on one diamond. /demos, once 6a ships.

S6-03 — The tournament’s own overlap refusal is a browser rule

Two windows refuse; drag, the rain-delay shift, the generator, the playoffs and the server skip it. Tournament Stage 3.

S6-04 — A tournament venue’s library link is written once and read by nothing

A clone and import-from-past drop it; a second import duplicates; the wizard searches other tournaments’ copies. 6a keeps the link; Tournament Stage 5 redraws the wizard.

S6-05 — A series edit leaves each date’s place link behind

The words change on every date, the link on none. 6a.

S6-06 — The tournament mirror writes into a team’s schedule on every read

A mirrored game is the tournament’s booking; the check skips it. 6a.

S6-07 — Nearly half of rep events have no end

119 of 259 on dev; counted as 90 minutes. Ask 3.

S6-08 — Deleting a library venue strips house league’s bookings

Archive when anything books it. 6b, Ask 9.

S6-09 — A failed library load reads as an empty library

Say so, with Try again. 6b.

S6-10 — Any member can write venues directly

The database’s rules allow it; members read, the server writes. 6b.

S6-11 — The Organization page’s Venues tile has no plan gate

And a second name. 6b.

S6-12 — The public league schedule groups weeks by the server’s clock

UTC on the host. Ask 8, in 6b.

S6-13 — No org records a time zone or a province

A platform item before the first club outside Eastern time.

E00 — Families is live and unwalked

The whole area reached production without its owner walks. Stage 5.

E01 — A merge undoes itself

The next read re-mints a ghost person for the merged address, who can be proposed again and messaged at the old address. Stage 5.

E02 — A changed guardian email strands the child

The child stays with the old person and messages go to the old address; the new address becomes a stranger. Stage 5.

E03 — Family money disagrees with the Money hub

Paid and unpaid are read from a stamp that only exists when an installment is fully paid, so partial payments vanish. Stage 5.

E04 — The export overclaims

It says "everything this organization holds" and carries a page's worth. Stage 5.

F01 — The tryouts card loops home

It links to a teams route that is only a redirect; the tryout's own address is already loaded and unused. Stage 0.

F02 — Rep teams are publicly invisible

No index, no link from anywhere, not in the sitemap or search. Stage 4.

F03 — The home page is tournament-first

An empty "no active tournaments" block leads the page fifty weeks a year. Stage 4.

F06 — Public team and tryout pages skip the checks other pages make

A cancelled or private club keeps serving team pages and tryout forms until the family submits. Stage 4.

F07 — Any org's archive can be shown under another org's name

The archive page loads by id alone. Stage 0.

F10 — Marketing promises what does not exist

Coming soon, parent notifications, field bookings, invoicing, reconciliation, a stale README price. Stage 4 / 8.

G01 — A "first tournament setup" banner forever

It shows whenever a club has no tournament and links to the house-league wizard. Stage 7.

G02 — No way to message every family

Tournament comms reach registered teams' coaches; league broadcast is per season; coach announcements per team; Families one household at a time. Stage 7.

G03 — The club's own team enters its own event in two steps

One-click works for coach-portal orgs only. Stage 7.

H01 — Nothing proves the club side works

No club browser suite, no admin routes in the layout sweep, no club demo, a fixture with two people and no teams. Stage 8.

I01 — A tenant-boundary hole in house league

Draft and placement routes accept division, registration and team ids from the request and return or rewrite other clubs' registrations, guardian contacts included. Stage 0 security sweep.

I02 — The admin is told about the wrong registrations

The "new registration" notice fires on a manual add, never on a parent's submission. Stage 9.

I04 — Deletes silently cascade

Deleting a team or division deletes its games and results; season changes fire in one click. Stage 9.

Stage 2 · findings drawn on the mockups

Headings for every finding a Stage 2 specimen flags that the lists above did not already carry (drawn 2026-09-28). The S2- rows were found while drawing; the others are plan §4B rows, ruling D10 and the June J4 findings Stage 2 closes (§11).

B07 — The tryout lifecycle contradicts itself

The admin can open tryouts and accept a player onto a closed season; the public page and the sign-up form use different rules for which season takes sign-ups; the coach and the admin act on different seasons; stale copy on the page and in coach help. Stage 2, specimen 7.

B09 — The club-side team page is thin

No edit for name, division, colour or group, no un-archive, and a save that ignores the group; a false “empty coach list” sentence; an Assign panel on finished seasons whose saves are refused. Stage 2, specimens 2, 3 and 5.

B10 — Access is still read from season rows in places

Stage 3b · findings drawn on the mockups

Headings for every finding a Stage 3b specimen flags that the lists above did not already carry (drawn 2026-10-05). The S3B- rows were found in that pass, except S3B-06, which is carried from the plan so the build can't miss it; the J4 rows are the June audit's, re-verified that day.

S3B-01 — Club spending would meet the plan by line, the coach's meets it by word

A coach's cost carries a budget category and word, and Budget vs. Actual matches spending to the plan by the word; a word carries one line on a plan (owner, 2026-09-09). A club ledger line carries only a free-text category, and the plan's 3b list would add a budget line to it. Ask 4a.

S3B-02 — The club's plan holds spending only

The add-line form fixes every line to money out (“there isn't one” revenue surface); no ruling made it so. Sponsors, grants and fundraising have no line to be read against. Ask 4b.

S3B-03 — Two rules on the Budget tab

Lines and periods are owner or treasurer by name; the Allocate page refuses an admin whom its own route accepts under 3a's one rule. Ask 4d.

S3B-04 — The coach is never told what the club reads

3b makes the club read a team's cash on hand. The club's “What the club sees” panel doesn't list it and the portal says nothing of what the club reads. Ask 4c.

S3B-05 — A team's standing has two homes

Budget vs. Actual's team-health cards work it out themselves (all years against one, “Behind” under 50%) beside 3a's single definition on the Overview, Allocations and a team's account; each card opens the whole Rep Teams board. Specimen 2: the cards leave for the summary.

S3B-06 — The shared-payee report has its data and no screen

Defined in the plan on 2026-10-02 (D1 widened narrowly) with its data in mig 316; the coach's payee list already says the club sees these payments. Specimen 5, Ask 3.

J4-024 — Budget vs. Actual has no actuals

June audit, re-verified 2026-10-05: no Actual for any line, and the screen promises “a future update”. Specimen 2, Ask 4a.

J4-025 — A headroom that stops at fifty rows

June audit, re-verified 2026-10-05: unchanged. One Headroom from every row, shown once on the summary.

J4-026 — The budget plan's arithmetic

June audit, re-verified 2026-10-05: one allocation per line, the rest stranded, totals that can drop under what is allocated. Specimen 1.

J4-028 — The club's net position includes money that isn't the club's

June audit, re-verified 2026-10-05: the Overview's four figures add every book, the teams' included. Specimen 3, Ask 1.

Stage 3c · findings drawn on the mockups

Headings for every finding a Stage 3c specimen flags that the lists above did not already carry (drawn 2026-10-07, from the code read that day). C10 and C17 are above; their 3c re-reading is in the finding's window.

S3C-01 — The year is worked out in a dozen places, not one

Three definitions read the year, nine screen readings work it out by hand (two from UTC timestamps), and the gate, the seed and the tests hard-code January. 3b's note said one place. The build routes every reading through one definition. Specimen 2.

S3C-02 — By period's quarters are calendar quarters

A September year would read five part-quarters. The club's quarters start at its first month; the coach's are unchanged. Specimen 2.

S3C-03 — The payee report matches a team season's number to the club year's

A year named 2025–26 has no single number; the build lists a team with a season numbered for either calendar year the club's year touches. Specimen 7.

S3C-04 — A season stores no dates

A year number, a name and a status; its start is its row's creation time and its "close date" is its last change. Nothing in 3c asks a season for its dates. Read first.

S3C-05 — An unpaid club bill leaves the coach's Club tab when its season rolls over

The Club tab reads the working season's bills; after the roll the old bill is on no live coach screen except a lane whose door leads back to the tab. A September year makes it ordinary. Ask 8b, specimen 8.

S3C-06 — "Ledgers archive at year-end" is the wrong goal

Nothing archives a book, and a club book runs across years. A year-end locks dates; archiving a finished tournament's book is Stage 7's. Ask 8a.

S3C-07 — Four corrections change a line where it sits

Undo, Reverse, Void and clearing a cheque would each move a closed year's locked figures. Refused on a closed year's line, pointing at Reopen. Ask 8d, specimen 3.

S3C-08 — A year can't stay a four-digit number

A change of first month makes two years share a number however it is keyed. The build's migration adds a row per club year. Not drawn.

S3C-09 — New allocation offers a team's closed seasons

Every season, worded with the database's status, and the server checks only that it is the team's. Only open seasons, under the word Season; the server refuses a closed one. Specimen 6.

S3C-10 — The payee window opens straight into an editable name

No reading state, and the report is a page one level down. The window reads first with the report as its body. Ask 7, specimen 7.

S3C-11 — A late payment of an old season’s club bill lands in the closed season

Found writing the build prompts (2026-10-07): the coach’s register counts a club bill’s payment in the bill’s season, so a payment after that season closed moves a closed season’s figures. Ruled the same day: the season running when the payment is recorded carries it; a past season is adjusted by reopening it (only while no season is running) and recording the payment there.
